timeline.title: Vercel 收购 NuxtLabs
timeline.subtitle: 涉及 Nuxt、Nitro。这是 Vue 生态的重要全栈框架和服务端运行基础设施，Nuxt 原作者 Sébastien Chopin 等核心团队进入 Vercel。

en.title: Vercel Acquires NuxtLabs
en.subtitle: The acquisition involves Nuxt and Nitro, important full-stack framework and server-runtime infrastructure in the Vue ecosystem. Core team members, including Nuxt creator Sébastien Chopin, join Vercel.

timeline.title: Databricks 收购 Electric
timeline.subtitle: Electric 团队加入 Databricks 并入 Neon；涉及可在浏览器等环境运行的轻量 Postgres——PGlite，以及 Postgres 实时读同步层 Electric Sync。

en.title: Databricks Acquires Electric
en.subtitle: The Electric team joins Databricks and becomes part of Neon. Its technologies include PGlite, a lightweight Postgres that runs in browsers and other environments, and Electric Sync, a real-time read synchronization layer for Postgres.

timeline.title: AWS 收购 Duckdb
timeline.subtitle: 签约收购的是 DuckDB 背后的 DuckLabs 公司及团队，创始人 Hannes Mühleisen、Mark Raasveldt 继续带队；DuckDB 开源项目不在收购范围内，仍由独立基金会管理。

en.title: AWS Acquires DuckLabs, the Company Behind DuckDB
en.subtitle: The agreement covers DuckLabs and its team, with founders Hannes Mühleisen and Mark Raasveldt continuing to lead it. The open-source DuckDB project is not included in the acquisition and remains managed by an independent foundation.

timeline.title: Cloudflare 收购 VoidZero
timeline.subtitle: 涉及 Vite、Vitest、Rolldown、Oxc、Vite+；尤雨溪及 VoidZero 团队加盟 Cloudflare，继续主导这些项目，项目保持 MIT 开源。

en.title: Cloudflare Acquires VoidZero
en.subtitle: The acquisition involves Vite, Vitest, Rolldown, Oxc, and Vite+. Evan You and the VoidZero team join Cloudflare and continue leading these projects, which remain open-source under the MIT license.

timeline.title: Supabase 收购 Turso
timeline.subtitle: 涉及 SQLite 兼容数据库 Turso，创始人 Glauber Costa 加入 Supabase，负责 Agent 相关服务；Turso 不取代 Postgres，双方产品暂时独立。

en.title: Supabase Acquires Turso
en.subtitle: The acquisition involves the SQLite-compatible Turso database. Founder Glauber Costa joins Supabase to lead agent-related services. Turso does not replace Postgres, and the two products initially remain separate.

timeline.title: Cloudflare 收购  Deno
timeline.subtitle: Node.js 与 Deno 创始人 Ryan Dahl 及 Deno 全体团队加盟 Cloudflare，携 celld 参与 Workers 和 Durable Objects 研发；Deno Runtime 再维护一年后停止官方开发，Deno Deploy 六个月后关闭。

en.title: Cloudflare Acquires Deno
en.subtitle: Node.js and Deno creator Ryan Dahl and the entire Deno team join Cloudflare, bringing celld to the development of Workers and Durable Objects. Official Deno Runtime development will end after one more year of maintenance, and Deno Deploy will close after six months.

timeline.title: Cloudflare 收购 Astro
timeline.subtitle: 涉及 Astro 网站框架；The Astro Technology Company 全体全职员工加入 Cloudflare，继续开发 Astro，项目保持 MIT 开源、公开路线图与开放治理。

en.title: Cloudflare Acquires Astro
en.subtitle: The acquisition involves the Astro web framework. All full-time employees of The Astro Technology Company join Cloudflare and continue developing Astro, which retains its MIT license, public roadmap, and open governance.

timeline.title: Databricks 收购 Neon
timeline.subtitle: 交易金额约 10 亿美元，标的是 Serverless Postgres 公司 Neon；其数据库采用计算与存储分离架构，Neon 团队在交易完成后加入 Databricks。

en.title: Databricks Acquires Neon
en.subtitle: The approximately $1 billion deal targets Neon, a serverless Postgres company whose database separates compute from storage. The Neon team joins Databricks after the transaction closes.

timeline.title: Anthropic 收购 Bun
timeline.subtitle: JavaScript 运行时与开发工具 Bun 的创始人 Jarred Sumner 及团队加入 Anthropic；Bun 用于 Claude Code 与 Claude Agent SDK，继续由原团队维护，保持 MIT 开源。

en.title: Anthropic Acquires Bun
en.subtitle: Bun creator Jarred Sumner and his team join Anthropic. The JavaScript runtime and development toolkit is used by Claude Code and the Claude Agent SDK, continues to be maintained by its original team, and remains MIT-licensed open source.

timeline.title: Cloudflare 开源 Workers 运行时 workerd
timeline.subtitle: 发布 workerd 首个 Beta 版本：与 Cloudflare Workers 使用同源代码的 JavaScript/Wasm 服务器运行时，以 Apache-2.0 许可证开源，可用于自托管应用、本地开发与测试。

en.title: Cloudflare Open-Sources the Workers Runtime, workerd
en.subtitle: Cloudflare releases the first beta of workerd, a JavaScript/Wasm server runtime built from the same source code as Cloudflare Workers. Released under Apache-2.0, it supports self-hosted applications, local development, and testing.

timeline.title: Ryan Dahl 发布 Node.js
timeline.subtitle: Ryan Dahl 发布基于 V8 的 JavaScript 运行时 Node.js，以事件驱动、非阻塞 I/O 支持服务器端网络应用。

en.title: Ryan Dahl Releases Node.js
en.subtitle: Ryan Dahl releases Node.js, a JavaScript runtime built on V8 that supports server-side network applications with an event-driven, non-blocking I/O model.

timeline.title: Cloudflare 宣布推出 Workers
timeline.subtitle: 首次公布 Workers：把 JavaScript 计算带到 Cloudflare 全球边缘网络，采用类似 Service Workers 的接口，让开发者编写请求处理逻辑。

en.title: Cloudflare Announces Workers
en.subtitle: Cloudflare first announces Workers, bringing JavaScript compute to its global edge network with an interface similar to Service Workers, so developers can write request-handling logic.

timeline.title: Ryan Dahl 首次公开介绍 Deno
timeline.subtitle: Node.js 创造者 Ryan Dahl 在 JSConf EU 演讲中介绍 Deno：重新思考 JavaScript 运行时的安全、模块管理与 TypeScript 支持。

en.title: Ryan Dahl Introduces Deno Publicly
en.subtitle: Node.js creator Ryan Dahl introduces Deno in a talk at JSConf EU, rethinking security, module management, and TypeScript support in a JavaScript runtime.

timeline.title: AWS 发布 Lambda
timeline.subtitle: AWS 在 re:Invent 2014 推出 Lambda 预览版：按事件运行代码，自动管理计算资源，按请求和计算时长计费，无需预先配置或管理服务器。

en.title: AWS Launches Lambda
en.subtitle: AWS introduces a preview of Lambda at re:Invent 2014: code runs in response to events, compute resources are managed automatically, and billing is based on requests and execution time, without provisioning or managing servers in advance.

timeline.title: Deno 发布开源项目 celld v0.1.0
timeline.subtitle: 发布可自托管的分布式 Durable Objects 项目 celld，让开发者在自己的机器上运行 Workers 与有状态对象，并使用自行管理的存储保存数据。

en.title: Deno Releases the Open-Source celld Project, v0.1.0
en.subtitle: Deno releases celld, a self-hostable distributed Durable Objects project that lets developers run Workers and stateful objects on their own machines and persist data in storage they manage themselves.

timeline.title: Facebook 启动 TAO 开发
timeline.subtitle: Facebook 基础设施团队于 2009 年初开始开发 TAO（The Associations and Objects），将对象与关联关系抽象实现为专门的分布式数据服务，改善原有客户端实现的缓存一致性、增量更新与数据传输问题。

en.title: Facebook Begins Developing TAO
en.subtitle: In early 2009, Facebook’s infrastructure team begins developing TAO (The Associations and Objects). It implements object and association abstractions as a dedicated distributed data service to address cache consistency, incremental update, and data transfer problems in the existing client-side implementation.

ja.title: Facebook が TAO の開発を開始
ja.subtitle: 2009 年初め、Facebook のインフラチームが TAO（The Associations and Objects）の開発を開始。オブジェクトと関連の抽象化を専用の分散データサービスとして実装し、従来のクライアント側の実装にあったキャッシュの整合性、差分更新、データ転送の問題を改善する。

timeline.title: React 团队首次公开展示 RSC（React Server Components）研究原型
timeline.subtitle: React 团队公开 React Server Components（RSC）的演讲、演示与 RFC，探索组件在服务器执行、直接访问服务端数据且不向浏览器发送其组件实现代码的架构。当时仍处于研究与开发阶段；此日期是首次公开研究，不是稳定版本发布日期。

en.title: The React Team Presents Its First React Server Components Research Prototype
en.subtitle: The React team publishes a talk, demo, and RFC for React Server Components (RSC), exploring an architecture in which components execute on the server and access server-side data directly without sending their implementation code to the browser. The work is still in research and development; this date marks the first public research presentation, not a stable release.

ja.title: React チームが React Server Components の研究プロトタイプを初公開
ja.subtitle: React チームが React Server Components（RSC）の講演、デモ、RFC を公開。コンポーネントをサーバーで実行し、その実装コードをブラウザーに送らずにサーバー側のデータへ直接アクセスする構成を探る。当時は研究開発段階であり、この日付は研究の初公開を示すもので、安定版の公開日ではない。

timeline.title: GitHub GraphQL API 正式可用
timeline.subtitle: GitHub 宣布 GraphQL API 结束 Early Access，面向开发者正式提供类型化的关联数据查询接口，以更少请求获取应用所需的数据。

en.title: GitHub’s GraphQL API Becomes Generally Available
en.subtitle: GitHub announces that its GraphQL API has left Early Access, offering developers a typed interface for querying related data and retrieving application data with fewer requests.

timeline.title: Facebook 公开介绍 TAO 社交图数据服务
timeline.subtitle: Facebook 发表技术文章，公开介绍 TAO 的对象与关联关系模型、API，以及基于 MySQL 和分布式缓存的数据访问架构，并回顾其在内部的开发和运行经验。

en.title: Facebook Introduces the TAO Social Graph Data Service
en.subtitle: Facebook publishes a technical article introducing TAO’s object-and-association model, API, and data access architecture built on MySQL and distributed caching. It also looks back on the system’s internal development and operational experience.

ja.title: Facebook がソーシャルグラフデータサービス TAO を紹介
ja.subtitle: Facebook が技術記事を公開し、TAO のオブジェクトと関連のモデル、API、MySQL と分散キャッシュに基づくデータアクセスアーキテクチャを紹介。社内での開発・運用経験も振り返る。

timeline.title: GraphQL 在 Facebook 内部诞生
timeline.subtitle: Facebook 为原生移动应用的数据获取设计 GraphQL，以类型化查询描述客户端所需的对象与关系。

en.title: GraphQL Is Created Internally at Facebook
en.subtitle: Facebook designs GraphQL to fetch data for its native mobile applications, using typed queries to describe the objects and relationships clients need.

ja.title: Facebook 社内で GraphQL が誕生
ja.subtitle: Facebook がネイティブモバイルアプリのデータ取得のために GraphQL を設計。型付きクエリで、クライアントが必要とするオブジェクトと関係を記述する。

timeline.title: Facebook 公开介绍 Dragon 分布式图查询引擎
timeline.subtitle: Facebook 介绍 Dragon 如何在 TAO 数据访问基础上优化高吞吐、多跳社交图查询，减少查询执行中的网络与计算开销。此日期为官方技术文章的发表日期。

en.title: Facebook Introduces Dragon, a Distributed Graph Query Engine
en.subtitle: Facebook explains how Dragon builds on TAO data access to optimize high-throughput, multi-hop social graph queries, reducing network and computation overhead during execution. This date is the publication date of the official technical article.

timeline.title: Facebook 发布原生重构的 iOS 应用
timeline.subtitle: Facebook 从以 HTML5 为主的移动方案转向原生 iOS 实现，优化启动、滚动和数据加载。这是理解 GraphQL 早期移动端数据需求的历史背景。

en.title: Facebook Releases Its Rebuilt Native iOS Application
en.subtitle: Facebook moves from a mobile approach based primarily on HTML5 to a native iOS implementation, improving startup, scrolling, and data loading. This provides historical context for understanding GraphQL’s early mobile data requirements.

timeline.title: Facebook 开源 GraphQL 规范
timeline.subtitle: Facebook 对外发布首个 GraphQL 规范草案（July 2015），将内部的数据查询技术开放给开发者社区。

en.title: Facebook Open-Sources the GraphQL Specification
en.subtitle: Facebook releases the first public draft of the GraphQL specification (July 2015), opening its internal data-querying technology to the developer community.

ja.title: Facebook が GraphQL 仕様をオープンソース化
ja.subtitle: Facebook が GraphQL 仕様の最初の公開草案（July 2015）を発表し、社内のデータクエリ技術を開発者コミュニティに公開。

timeline.title: Shopify 宣布将 GraphQL 确立为主要 API 方向
timeline.subtitle: Shopify 宣布将 REST Admin API 标记为 Legacy，并将新功能与改进集中于 GraphQL；公告要求自 2025 年 4 月 1 日起新提交的公开应用采用 GraphQL。

en.title: Shopify Makes GraphQL Its Primary API Direction
en.subtitle: Shopify announces that the REST Admin API will be designated Legacy, with new features and improvements focused on GraphQL. The announcement requires newly submitted public apps to use GraphQL from April 1, 2025.

timeline.title: Facebook 首次开源 Relay 技术预览版
timeline.subtitle: Facebook 首次开源 Relay 的技术预览版。这套面向 React 应用的数据框架通过 GraphQL 声明组件的数据需求，统一处理查询批处理、异步数据获取、缓存和视图更新；当时仍有尚未完成的功能。

en.title: Facebook Open-Sources the First Relay Technical Preview
en.subtitle: Facebook releases the first open-source technical preview of Relay. This data framework for React applications uses GraphQL to declare components’ data requirements and coordinates query batching, asynchronous data fetching, caching, and view updates. Some features are still incomplete at this stage.

ja.title: Facebook が Relay 初の技術プレビュー版をオープンソース化
ja.subtitle: Facebook が Relay の技術プレビュー版を初めて公開。React アプリケーション向けのこのデータフレームワークは、GraphQL でコンポーネントのデータ要件を宣言し、クエリのバッチ処理、非同期データ取得、キャッシュ、ビューの更新を統合して扱う。当時は未完成の機能も残っていた。

timeline.title: Next.js 13 发布：App Router 测试版集成 RSC 与流式渲染
timeline.subtitle: Next.js 13 的新 app 目录以测试版推出，集成 React Server Components、布局、组件级异步数据获取及 Streaming。稳定的 Next.js 13／pages 路由与测试中的 app 路由需要区分；当时官方尚不建议将 app 目录用于生产。

en.title: Next.js 13 Introduces an App Router Beta with RSC and Streaming
en.subtitle: Next.js 13 launches its new app directory in beta, integrating React Server Components, layouts, component-level asynchronous data fetching, and streaming. The stable Next.js 13/pages router must be distinguished from the beta app router; production use of the app directory is not yet recommended at this point.

timeline.title: Next.js 13.4 发布：App Router 核心进入稳定阶段
timeline.subtitle: Next.js 13.4 宣布 App Router 核心可用于生产，覆盖 RSC、布局、数据获取及 Streaming／Suspense。这标志着框架层面的稳定采用；当时基于 React Canary，Server Actions 仍为 Alpha，并不等于 React 所有服务端能力同时稳定。

en.title: Next.js 13.4 Stabilizes the Core App Router
en.subtitle: Next.js 13.4 announces that the core App Router is production-ready, covering RSC, layouts, data fetching, and Streaming/Suspense. This marks stable framework adoption; it is based on React Canary, and Server Actions remain alpha. It does not mean every server-side React capability becomes stable simultaneously.

timeline.title: React 18 发布：Suspense 支持服务端流式渲染
timeline.subtitle: React 18 将 Suspense 扩展到服务端，新增 renderToPipeableStream 和 renderToReadableStream，使已就绪的界面可先行流式交付。React 官方同时说明 Server Components 仍在实验阶段，不能把 React 18 的流式 SSR 发布写成 RSC 已稳定。

en.title: React 18 Adds Server-Side Streaming with Suspense
en.subtitle: React 18 extends Suspense to the server with renderToPipeableStream and renderToReadableStream, allowing ready parts of the interface to stream first. React’s announcement also states that Server Components remain experimental; the streaming SSR release should not be described as stable RSC.

timeline.title: GraphQL.js v17 发布：提供实验性 @defer／@stream 增量执行支持
timeline.subtitle: GraphQL.js v17 正式发布，并通过 experimentalExecuteIncrementally 提供 @defer／@stream 的实验性增量执行支持。普通 execute 仍返回单一结果；相关提案和增量响应格式仍在演进，不能将参考实现中的实验支持写成规范已经定稿或各客户端已统一支持。

en.title: GraphQL.js v17 Adds Experimental @defer/@stream Incremental Execution
en.subtitle: GraphQL.js v17 is released with experimental @defer/@stream support through experimentalExecuteIncrementally. The ordinary execute function still returns a single result. The proposals and incremental response format continue to evolve; experimental support in the reference implementation does not mean the specification is final or that every client supports it consistently.

timeline.title: React 19 稳定发布：RSC 进入 React 稳定版本
timeline.subtitle: React 19 将此前 Canary 渠道的 Server Components 功能纳入稳定版本，并支持 Server Actions。官方明确：React 19 中的 RSC 功能稳定，但供打包器和框架实现 RSC 的底层 API 仍不遵循语义版本保证，可能在次版本间变化。

en.title: React 19 Becomes Stable, Bringing RSC into a Stable React Release
en.subtitle: React 19 incorporates Server Components previously available through Canary and supports Server Actions. React clarifies that RSC features are stable in React 19, but the underlying APIs for bundlers and frameworks implementing RSC do not yet follow semantic-versioning guarantees and may change between minor releases.

timeline.title: React 16.6 发布：通过 React.lazy 与 Suspense 支持客户端代码分割
timeline.subtitle: React 16.6 正式提供 React.lazy，让客户端以 Suspense 边界协调懒加载组件的备用界面。此次能力面向代码分割，尚不支持服务端 Suspense；不能把它与后来的流式 SSR 或 RSC 稳定发布混为一谈。

en.title: React 16.6 Adds Client-Side Code Splitting with React.lazy and Suspense
en.subtitle: React 16.6 introduces React.lazy, allowing clients to coordinate fallbacks for lazy-loaded components with Suspense boundaries. This release targets code splitting and does not yet support server-side Suspense; it should not be confused with later streaming SSR or stable RSC releases.

timeline.title: GraphQL 公布 @defer／@stream 实验实现与标准化进展
timeline.subtitle: GraphQL 官方博客介绍 @defer 与 @stream 如何分批交付查询结果，并公布 GraphQL.js 和 express-graphql 的实验版本供社区反馈。当时提案处于 Stage 2；这是公开实验和标准化进展，不是增量交付规范正式定稿。

en.title: GraphQL Publishes Experimental @defer/@stream Implementations and a Standardization Update
en.subtitle: The official GraphQL blog explains how @defer and @stream deliver query results in parts and announces experimental GraphQL.js and express-graphql releases for community feedback. The proposal is at Stage 2; this is a public experiment and standardization update, not a finalized incremental-delivery specification.

events.title: 重新理解 GraphQL - 06：重新评价 GraphQL——被误用、被高估，还是被低估？
events.subtitle: 从 Facebook 的设计哲学到现实中的工程困境

en.title: Rethinking GraphQL - 06: Reassessing GraphQL—Misused, Overrated, or Underrated?
en.subtitle: From Facebook’s design philosophy to the engineering challenges of real-world adoption

text.text: Which strengths of GraphQL as a standalone technology should not be overlooked?
How much of Relay’s design philosophy can be adopted independently?
Can other companies reproduce the benefits of Facebook’s broader system?
GraphQL’s prerequisites, engineering costs, and practical limits.
Returning to the original debate: where do GraphQL’s real problems lie?
This chapter examines GraphQL’s historical value, its value today, and its future applicability.
The first five chapters covered GraphQL’s origins, Relay’s philosophy, Facebook’s backend infrastructure, problems in industry practice, and changes introduced by architectures such as RSC.
We can now return to the initial question: why do some teams adopt GraphQL without fully realizing the expected benefits, while increasing system complexity?
Answering this requires separating three frequently conflated ideas:
GraphQL’s value as a query language and API specification.
The engineering capabilities provided by client frameworks such as Relay.
The performance and scalability benefits of Facebook’s overall data infrastructure.
They are closely related, but not every advantage of the latter two belongs to GraphQL. Equally, inability to reproduce Facebook’s complete system does not negate GraphQL’s standalone value.
1. What Is GraphQL’s Standalone Value?
Its central innovation is not an individual feature impossible with REST. It organizes related data access capabilities into a common language and specification.
The most important capabilities include:
First, typed client queries declare the required data structure.

Within the schema, clients select fields, supply arguments, and follow business-object relationships. They can compose data for their actual needs instead of depending entirely on fixed server-designed responses.

REST can provide similar effects through parameterized interfaces and aggregation, but GraphQL supplies a common language rather than requiring every API to invent its own selection and composition mechanisms.
Second, the schema defines a contract across clients and languages.

The type system describes objects, fields, arguments, and relationships, not just return values. Clients can discover the schema through introspection and use tooling for code generation, type checking, exploration, and documentation.
Technologies such as OpenAPI also provide typed contracts. GraphQL closely connects type definitions to its client query language, letting the schema validate queries themselves.
Third, fragments provide a language foundation for composing requirements.

Fragments do not automatically imply component-level dependency management, but they offer reusable, composable field selections. Relay uses this to integrate declarations into React component organization.
Fourth, clients and servers can evolve independently around one schema.
Servers can generally add fields without affecting old clients that do not request them. Clients can select new combinations as their needs change.
This matters for services shared by web, iOS, Android, and third-party applications.

GraphQL does not guarantee backward compatibility for every schema change or eliminate version management. Shopify’s GraphQL Admin API, for example, explicitly uses versioning. GraphQL supports gradual evolution; it does not prohibit versioned architectures.
Together, these features form GraphQL’s standalone value: a unified, typed, composable query contract for complex business data that can evolve continuously.
That is more complete than saying clients can choose fields, and more accurate than describing GraphQL as a complete data management architecture.
2. GraphQL Can Succeed Without Facebook’s Complete Technology Stack
GraphQL has an independent ecosystem beyond Facebook. GitHub and Shopify are particularly informative examples.
GitHub: Flexible Queries for External Developers
GitHub offers both REST and GraphQL APIs.

Its official documentation explains that GraphQL gives API consumers more flexible selection and composition, reducing repeated requests for related data. GitHub also limits query cost, node counts, execution time, and resource consumption.
API consumers benefit from a common schema, complex relationship queries, and selecting data for their integration needs. They do not need Relay or knowledge of GitHub’s internal database caches.
Shopify: GraphQL as the Main Business API
In 2024, Shopify made GraphQL its primary API direction and designated the REST Admin API Legacy. New features and improvements increasingly focus on GraphQL.

Shopify serves many third-party developers working with products, orders, inventory, customers, and marketing. GraphQL is a public business-data interface here, not merely an internal React data management tool.
Its practice also shows that flexibility requires server-side constraints.
The GraphQL Admin API uses cost-based rate limiting, assigning costs to fields and collections and regulating access according to the resources a query requires.
These cases demonstrate two points:
Successful GraphQL adoption does not require reproducing Facebook’s complete stack.
Standalone value is not free either. As scale and openness increase, query governance becomes necessary infrastructure.
3. Relay’s Real Lesson Extends Beyond Using GraphQL
If we do not attribute every Relay feature to GraphQL, what remains worth learning? Its approach to managing data dependencies.
Traditional component development emphasizes UI independence, but independent maintenance of data requirements also affects large-project maintainability.

Relay colocates fragments with components, uses data masking to restrict undeclared dependencies, analyzes and validates dependencies through its compiler, and coordinates shared entity access through normalized caching and subscriptions.
Together, these express a principle: components should own not only their UI implementation but also clear, checkable data dependency boundaries.
The implications for complex frontend applications extend beyond GraphQL.

REST or RPC applications can also declare component data requirements explicitly, maintain contracts through generated types, and share repeated data through common caches. RSC can place server access logic near components as well.

Relay’s distinctive foundation is that GraphQL fragments supply a common, statically analyzable declaration format. Its compiler can validate and transform queries during builds. Similar ideas implemented with other technologies may not have identical static-analysis capabilities or tooling.
More broadly, Relay demonstrates that explicit dependencies managed and analyzed by shared tools can deliver deeper frontend benefits than network-request optimization alone.
Apollo’s support for fragment colocation, useFragment, and data masking also reflects the wider value of these ideas.
Constraints always have trade-offs. Consistent conventions may reduce long-term costs in large teams while adding unnecessary tools and access rules to simple projects.
4. Facebook’s Backend Lesson: Abstraction Cannot Replace Execution Capabilities
Another lesson is separating the expression of requirements from their execution.
GraphQL lets clients describe objects and relationships. Servers must still decide which records to read, how to batch related access, and how to avoid repetition through caching.
Facebook’s TAO, Ent, and Loader provide these capabilities at different layers:
TAO optimizes frequent access and distributed caching around social graph objects and associations.
Ent combines business-entity access with loading and permission checks.
Loader reduces duplicate entity queries through batching and caching.
Other companies need not reproduce TAO or Ent. Relational databases, ORMs, Redis, DataLoader, and mature business logic can form a suitable system at their own scale.
The product names matter less than whether these questions are addressed:
Can multiple fields reuse or batch the same data?
Can relationships across objects be queried efficiently?
Are cache invalidation and consistency policies explicit?
Does a shared access or business layer enforce permissions?
Can complex queries be costed, limited, and monitored?
This explains why simply wrapping REST services in GraphQL may not improve performance. Execution capabilities must match business complexity; Facebook-scale infrastructure is not mandatory.
5. Which Scenarios Actually Suit GraphQL?
Adoption should be evaluated against the system’s overall construction and maintenance costs.

On the frontend, GraphQL can reduce page composition work and improve type generation and component dependencies. More complete approaches such as Relay also require maintaining schemas, compilation tooling, fragments, cache updates, and development conventions.
On the backend, it can reduce repeated aggregation endpoints for different clients while adding costs for resolvers, complexity controls, schema governance, authorization, and performance tracing.
Organizationally, a common schema can improve collaboration while requiring field ownership, interface review, and cross-service change coordination.

text.text: 6. Conclusion: An Independent Technology and a Foundation for Broader Engineering Ideas
GraphQL’s development since 2012 reveals three layers of value.
The first is GraphQL’s own API design.
A common schema, typed contracts, hierarchical queries, field selection, and fragments coordinate complex client–server requirements.
That standalone value does not depend on Relay or Facebook’s internal infrastructure.
The second is the component-level data management approach demonstrated by Relay.
Fragment colocation, data masking, compilation, and normalization integrate dependencies into component organization and maintenance.

This shows that GraphQL features can support capabilities deeper than ordinary API queries. But those benefits come from cooperation with additional tools and conventions, not from the language alone.
The third is Facebook’s backend infrastructure.
TAO, Ent, and Loader embody years of engineering around entities, relationships, loading, permissions, and distributed caching.
They support Facebook’s complex access needs but are not required parts of GraphQL, nor do they imply that every company needs an equivalent system.

The initial explanations are therefore not mutually exclusive. GraphQL can indeed be understood too narrowly or adopted inappropriately. Teams using only its language, underusing dependency-management capabilities, or underestimating backend costs may realize limited benefits.
Facebook’s complete practice is also distinctive. Not all its engineering advantages are inherent GraphQL capabilities, and every GraphQL project should not be expected to replicate it.
GraphQL should neither be dismissed as an overengineered REST replacement nor treated as the default best answer for complex applications because of Facebook’s success.
Adopting GraphQL is a concrete architectural choice. Understanding the ideas behind GraphQL, Relay, and Facebook’s infrastructure is a broader engineering education.

text.text: GraphQL 作为独立技术，究竟有哪些不可忽略的优势？
Relay 的设计哲学在多大程度上可以独立借鉴？
普通公司能否复制 Facebook 的体系化收益？
GraphQL 的适用条件、工程成本与实际边界。
回答最初的争论：GraphQL 真正的问题究竟在哪里？
本章回答：GraphQL 的历史价值、当前价值以及未来的适用边界。
前面五章分别讨论了 GraphQL 的诞生、Relay 的设计哲学、Facebook 的后端基础设施、业界实践中的工程问题，以及 RSC 等新架构带来的变化。
现在可以回到文章最初的问题：
为什么一些团队引入 GraphQL 后，并没有充分获得预期收益，却增加了系统复杂度？
要回答这个问题，首先需要区分三个经常被混为一谈的概念：
GraphQL 作为查询语言与 API 规范的价值。
Relay 等客户端框架所提供的工程能力。
Facebook 整体数据基础设施带来的性能与规模化收益。
它们之间存在密切联系，但不能把后两者的全部优势都归功于 GraphQL，也不能因为无法复制 Facebook 的完整体系，就否定 GraphQL 作为独立技术的价值。
一、GraphQL 的独立价值究竟是什么？
GraphQL 的核心创新，不是单独实现了某项 REST 无法完成的功能，而是将一组相互关联的数据访问能力，组织为统一的语言和规范。
其中最重要的能力包括：
第一，客户端通过类型化查询声明所需的数据结构。
GraphQL 允许客户端在 Schema 的约束下选择字段、指定参数，并沿着业务对象之间的关系组织查询。这使客户端能够根据实际使用场景组合数据，而不必完全依赖服务端预先设计好的固定响应结构。
REST 也可以通过参数化接口和聚合服务实现类似效果，但 GraphQL 为此提供了统一的查询语言，而不是要求不同 API 分别设计自己的字段选择和数据组合机制。
第二，Schema 提供跨客户端、跨语言的数据契约。
GraphQL 的类型系统不仅用于描述返回值，还明确了对象、字段、参数及其关系。客户端可以通过自省机制获取 Schema，再利用相关工具完成代码生成、类型检查、接口探索和文档构建。
OpenAPI 等技术同样能够实现类型化 API 契约，但 GraphQL 将类型定义与客户端查询语言紧密结合，使查询本身也能够受到 Schema 的验证。
第三，Fragment 为数据需求的组合提供了语言基础。
Fragment 并不必然意味着组件级数据依赖管理，但它提供了可复用、可组合的字段选择机制。Relay 正是利用这一特性，将数据依赖声明进一步融入 React 组件的组织方式。
第四，客户端和服务器可以围绕同一个 Schema 独立演进。
服务器通常可以添加字段，而不影响尚未查询这些字段的旧客户端。客户端也可以随着自身需求变化，选择新的字段组合。
这对于 Web、iOS、Android 及第三方应用共同使用的数据服务具有实际价值。
不过，GraphQL 并不能保证所有 Schema 变更都向后兼容，也不意味着应用不再需要版本管理。例如，Shopify 的 GraphQL Admin API 就采用明确的版本管理机制。这说明 GraphQL 所提供的是渐进式演进的能力，而不是禁止版本化的架构约束。
将这些能力结合起来，GraphQL 的独立价值可以概括为：
它为复杂业务数据提供了一套统一、类型化、可组合、能够持续演进的查询契约。
这比“客户端可以自由选择字段”更加完整，也比将 GraphQL 描述为完整的数据管理架构更加准确。
二、GraphQL 不依赖 Facebook 的完整技术体系，也可以取得成功
GraphQL 在 Facebook 之外已经形成了独立的应用生态。GitHub 和 Shopify 的实践尤其值得关注。
GitHub：面向外部开发者的灵活数据查询。
GitHub 同时提供 REST API 和 GraphQL API。
GitHub 在其官方文档中明确说明，采用 GraphQL 的重要原因，是为 API 使用者提供更灵活的数据选择和组合能力，减少为获取关联信息而进行的多次请求。也对其 GraphQL API 设置查询成本、节点数量、执行时间和资源消耗限制。
对于 GitHub API 的使用者而言，价值主要来自统一 Schema、复杂对象关系查询，以及能够根据具体集成需求选择数据。这些使用者不需要采用 Relay，也不需要了解 GitHub 内部如何设计数据库缓存。
Shopify：将 GraphQL 作为主要的业务 API。
Shopify 在 2024 年将 GraphQL 确立为其主要 API 方向，并将 REST Admin API 标记为 Legacy。其新功能开发和 API 改进也逐渐集中于 GraphQL。
Shopify 面向大量第三方应用开发者，涉及商品、订单、库存、客户及营销等复杂业务数据。GraphQL 在这里承担的是公共业务数据接口的角色，而不只是某个 React 应用内部的数据管理工具。
不过，Shopify 的实践同样说明，GraphQL 的灵活性需要相应的服务端约束。
Shopify 的 GraphQL Admin API 采用基于查询成本的限流机制，对不同字段和数据集合计算成本，并根据请求所需资源限制访问量。
这些案例说明了：
GraphQL 的成功应用并不需要完整复制 Facebook 的技术栈。
GraphQL 的独立价值也不是免费的。随着服务规模和开放程度提高，查询治理会成为必要的基础设施。
三、Relay 的真正启示，不只是如何使用 GraphQL
如果不把 Relay 的所有能力都归功于 GraphQL，那么 Relay 还有什么值得借鉴？答案是它所体现的一套数据依赖管理思想。
传统的组件化开发主要关注 UI 结构的独立性，但组件能否独立维护数据需求，同样影响大型项目的可维护性。
Relay 通过 Fragment colocation，将数据需求声明与组件实现放在一起；通过 Data masking，限制组件对未声明数据的依赖；通过编译器，分析并验证组件之间的数据依赖；再通过规范化缓存与数据订阅机制，协调不同组件对相同业务实体的访问。
这些设计共同体现出一种工程原则：
组件不仅应该拥有自己的 UI 实现，也应该拥有清晰、可检查的数据依赖边界。
这对于复杂前端应用的意义，并不局限于 GraphQL。
例如，采用 REST 或 RPC 的应用，同样可以让组件拥有明确的数据需求声明，通过类型生成工具维护接口契约，利用共享缓存管理重复数据。RSC 也可以将服务端数据访问逻辑组织在组件附近。
Relay 的一个重要特点，是 GraphQL Fragment 提供了统一的、可静态分析的数据声明形式，使编译器能够在应用构建阶段验证和转换查询。使用其他技术实现相似的工程思想，未必具有完全相同的静态分析能力和工具链。
它更重要的意义在于证明：
当组件的数据依赖能够被明确声明，并由工具统一分析和管理时，前端工程可以获得比单纯优化网络请求更深层次的收益。
Apollo 近年来支持 Fragment colocation、
useFragment
和 Data masking，也在一定程度上反映了这套设计思想的普遍价值。
不过，工程约束始终具有两面性。对于大型团队，统一的数据管理规范可能降低长期维护成本；对于简单项目，同样的编译工具链和数据访问规则也可能增加不必要的复杂度。
四、Facebook 的后端经验：抽象不能替代执行能力
Facebook 后端体系提供的另一项重要启示，是
将数据需求的表达与实际执行方式分离。
GraphQL 允许客户端描述需要哪些对象及其关联信息。但服务器必须决定如何执行这些查询，包括读取哪些数据库记录、如何批量访问关联数据，以及如何通过缓存减少重复操作。
Facebook 的 TAO、Ent、Loader 等技术，分别在不同层次提供了这些能力：
TAO 通过面向社交图的对象与关联数据模型，优化高频数据访问和分布式缓存。
Ent 将业务实体访问与数据加载、权限检查等机制结合。
Loader 通过批量加载和缓存，减少业务代码分别访问实体时产生的重复数据查询。
普通公司并不需要复制 TAO 或 Ent：关系型数据库、ORM、Redis、DataLoader，以及成熟的服务端业务逻辑，完全可能构成适合自身规模的数据访问体系。
关键不在于使用什么产品，而在于能否合理解决以下几项问题：
多个字段需要相同数据时，能否复用或批量加载？
跨对象关系查询是否能够高效执行？
数据缓存是否具有明确的失效和一致性策略？
业务权限是否由统一的数据访问或业务逻辑层负责？
复杂查询是否能够进行成本估算、限制和监控？
这也说明了为什么将现有 REST 服务简单包装成 GraphQL，并不一定能够改善系统性能。
GraphQL 需要与业务复杂度相匹配的数据执行能力，而不是必须与 Facebook 同等规模的基础设施配套。
五、哪些场景真正适合 GraphQL？
GraphQL 是否值得采用，需要从整个系统的建设和维护成本进行评价。
在前端，GraphQL 可能减少页面的数据组合工作，改善类型生成与跨组件数据依赖管理。但采用 Relay 或其他较完整的数据管理方案，也意味着需要维护 Schema、编译工具链、Fragment、缓存更新机制及相应开发规范。
在后端，GraphQL 可能减少针对不同客户端重复开发聚合接口的工作。但同时可能增加 Resolver、查询复杂度管理、Schema 治理、权限控制和性能追踪等成本。
在组织层面，统一 Schema 能够改善跨团队协作，也可能引入字段所有权、接口审核及跨服务变更协调等治理需求。

cells.text: 多客户端共享复杂业务数据

如果项目的核心痛点来自大型前端应用的组件数据依赖管理，单独只使用基础的 GraphQL Query，收益不大。GraphQL 配合 Relay 或系统化 Fragment 实践将提供较高收益。
面向第三方开发者的开放平台
非常重视 Schema 的稳定性、文档与数据组合能力。
适合评估 GraphQL，尤其当外部应用的数据组合需求差异较大时
GraphQL 可作为聚合层，但需要完善查询规划和服务端治理
少量固定页面的内部系统

GraphQL 未必必要，REST 或 RPC 可能更简单

text.text: 六、最终结论：GraphQL 是一项独立技术，也是一套工程思想的重要基础
回顾 GraphQL 从 2012 年至今的发展，可以看到三个不同层面的价值。
第一个层面，是 GraphQL 本身的 API 设计。
它提供统一的 Schema、类型化数据契约、层级查询、字段选择和 Fragment 组合，适合解决复杂客户端与服务器之间的数据需求协调问题。
这是 GraphQL 作为独立技术的价值，不依赖 Relay 或 Facebook 的内部基础设施。
第二个层面，是 Relay 所体现的组件级数据管理思想。
通过 Fragment colocation、Data masking、编译器和规范化缓存，将数据依赖纳入前端组件的组织与维护过程。
这套实践说明，GraphQL 的语言特性能够支持比普通 API 查询更深入的工程能力。但这些收益来自 GraphQL 与额外工具和规范的协作，不能完全归功于查询语言本身。
第三个层面，是 Facebook 的后端数据基础设施。
TAO、Ent、Loader 等技术体现了长期围绕业务实体、关联关系、数据加载、权限和分布式缓存建立的工程能力。
这些能力支持了 Facebook 的复杂数据访问需求，但不是 GraphQL 的必要组成部分，也不意味着其他公司必须采用同等规模的技术体系。
因此，文章最初提出的解释，并不是完全对立的：GraphQL 的确存在被简化理解和不恰当采用的情况。部分团队只引入查询语言，未能充分利用其数据依赖管理能力，或者低估了服务端执行成本，可能因此获得有限收益。
但另一方面，Facebook 的完整实践也具有明显的特殊性。不能将其所有工程优势都视为 GraphQL 的固有能力，更不能要求每一个 GraphQL 项目都复制这套体系。
GraphQL 既不应该被简单评价为一项过度设计的 REST 替代品，也不应该因为 Facebook 的成功而被视为复杂应用的默认最优解。
是否使用 GraphQL，是一项具体的架构选择；理解 GraphQL、Relay 以及 Facebook 数据基础设施的设计思想，则是一项更广泛的工程学习。

en.title: Cloudflare’s Platform Ambitions: Astro, Vite, Deno, and the Race for AI-Era Software Infrastructure
en.subtitle: How three acquisitions connect frameworks, developer tools, and an open execution platform—and why AI coding makes developer entry points a new cloud battleground

text.text: Workers’ strategic position in Cloudflare’s business.
What Astro, VoidZero/Vite, and Deno each contribute.
Why Cloudflare supports self-hosting Workers.
The different paths taken by Cloudflare and Vercel.
How AI coding changes toolchains and deployment entry points.
Whether Workers is becoming a general application execution standard.
In less than ten months during 2026, Cloudflare completed three noteworthy transactions.
On January 16, The Astro Technology Company, creator of the widely used Astro framework, joined Cloudflare.
On June 4, VoidZero, led by Vue.js and Vite creator Evan You, joined. Its portfolio includes Vite, Vitest, Rolldown, Oxc, and Vite+.
On October 9, Node.js creator Ryan Dahl brought the Deno team to Cloudflare. They announced workerd/celld integration to support self-hosted distributed Workers and Durable Objects.
At first, the acquisitions seem loosely related.
Astro is a web framework, Vite a development/build toolchain, Deno a runtime and cloud platform, and celld a distributed execution system.
Many are not Cloudflare-exclusive. Astro and Vite support other clouds; celld even allows Workers-model applications without Cloudflare servers.
Why would a cloud-services business invest heavily in technologies usable outside its platform?
Looking at each deal separately does not explain much.
Together, and alongside investment in agents, Workers, and its developer platform, they reveal an emerging path:
Cloudflare is expanding from networking and compute into the entire development, build, and execution lifecycle.
As AI coding changes software production, this may signal a shift in cloud competition, not merely a broader product catalog.
1. Why Expand Upstream into Developer Tools?
Start with Cloudflare’s existing business.
Its early focus was CDN, DNS, DDoS protection, and web application firewalls, built on a global network processing enormous traffic volumes.
It expanded from security and acceleration into Zero Trust, connectivity, development platforms, and compute.
Workers was central to that transition.
Traditional CDNs cache and transport content; Workers executes applications on the network.
Cloudflare began participating in application execution, not simply delivering completed applications.
It added D1, R2, KV, Durable Objects, Queues, and Workflows around Workers.
Developers could execute logic with Workers, store structured data in D1, files in R2, and live state in Durable Objects.
This established the basic capabilities of a full backend platform.
Technical viability alone does not make developers choose a platform.
Many decisions precede deployment.
Teams choose frameworks, project tools, build and test workflows, runtimes, databases, and deployment integrations.
Those decisions influence each other.
A Next.js team may naturally choose Vercel because of integration. Applications using a cloud’s databases, queues, and authentication may stay because of migration costs.
The competition concerns workflows, not simply server prices.
Competing only once development is finished means confronting choices and habits already established.
Cloudflare therefore began moving upstream.
That clarifies the value of Astro and VoidZero.
2. Astro: From Infrastructure into Web Frameworks
Cloudflare announced the Astro team’s arrival in January 2026.
Astro is an open-source framework for content-driven sites, widely used for documentation, blogs, marketing, and other content applications.
It emphasizes server-generated HTML, less unnecessary client JavaScript, and fast loading, unlike frameworks primarily centered on client interaction.
Its islands architecture renders most content as lightweight HTML and loads client code only for interactive regions.
This aligns naturally with Cloudflare’s network-performance strengths.
Cloudflare delivers content quickly; Astro helps developers build lightweight, fast content sites.
But the strategic value extends further.
Astro also underpins application-generation and website-building platforms.
The acquisition announcement named Webflow Cloud and Wix Vibe, already using Astro on Cloudflare infrastructure to create and deploy customer sites.
Users therefore need not be professional frontend developers.
They may be businesses generating sites through SaaS or people building applications with AI assistance.
Astro then sits very early in software production.
Supporting it can improve development/deployment integration with Workers and expose more Astro users to Cloudflare infrastructure.
This does not imply making Astro Workers-exclusive.
Cloudflare explicitly committed to open source, MIT licensing, and cross-platform deployment.
Other clouds remain supported.
Rather than forcing adoption through a closed framework, Cloudflare seeks smoother integration that makes developers more likely to choose its cloud voluntarily.
Astro is thus one upstream entry point.
But a framework covers only part of development.
Influencing the underlying toolchain can reach beyond any single framework.
That brings us to VoidZero.
3. VoidZero/Vite: An Entry Point Beyond One Framework
VoidZero joined Cloudflare in June 2026.
Its strategic role differs from Astro’s.
Astro is a particular framework; Vite supplies development and build tools for many frameworks and applications.
Projects across Vue, React, Svelte, and other ecosystems can use Vite’s development server and build foundation.
It concerns starting projects, compiling modules, updating code, and producing deployable output, rather than designing pages.
VoidZero built a broader JavaScript toolchain around it.
Vitest handles tests, Rolldown bundling, and Oxc, Oxlint, and Oxfmt parsing, linting, and formatting. Vite+ aims to integrate these into one development experience.
Their reach extends well beyond one framework.
A developer need not use Astro or Vue to depend on the Vite ecosystem.
Cloudflare gains a role in fundamental JavaScript tooling.
Substantial collaboration with Workers already existed.
In 2024, Cloudflare worked with Vite on the Environment API to support server runtimes beyond Node.js in local development.
Its official Vite plugin subsequently connected local workflows to workerd.
Developers could run Workers code and access Durable Objects, D1, and related capabilities locally with less divergence from production.
This addresses a longstanding problem: inconsistent development and production environments.
Code that worked in local Node.js could previously fail on Workers because of API or runtime differences.
Environment API integration gives local development behavior closer to deployment.
The collaboration continues beyond that.
The 2026 announcement proposed building more of Cloudflare’s application toolchain on Vite.
The explored unified cf CLI would make cf dev, cf build, and cf deploy fit familiar Vite workflows.
This is different from making Vite Cloudflare-exclusive.
It committed to vendor neutrality, with common interfaces supporting other providers’ runtimes and deployment systems.
The aim is integrating Cloudflare’s experience into Vite, not abandoning Vite’s openness.
Commercially, this is an indirect acquisition channel.
Choosing Vite does not guarantee choosing Cloudflare.
But deeply integrated development, testing, and deployment can make Workers a more natural, lower-friction option.
AI coding may amplify that advantage.
4. Why AI Coding Raises the Strategic Value of Toolchains
Traditionally, human programmers organized code, configured environments, ran tests, and deployed applications.
Agents increasingly generate projects, edit code, install dependencies, start development servers, run tests, and iteratively fix errors.
Toolchain quality may therefore matter even more.
A human might build or test dozens of times daily; an iterating agent can repeat many operations in a short period.
Stable, fast tools with machine-readable errors can improve task efficiency.
The VoidZero announcement emphasized this change:
Fast, composable Vite, Vitest, Rolldown, and Oxlint suit frequent agent execution as well as human developers.
AI changes more than invocation counts.
It shortens the boundaries between production, deployment, and execution.
Traditional work often separates requirements, coding, testing, building, deployment, and operations.
An AI platform may turn a natural-language request into an application, preview, tests, and deployment automatically.
Development and deployment become parts of one interaction rather than independent workflows.
This changes when cloud providers compete for developers.
Previously, they mainly sought workloads after development.
If a coding platform selects the framework, tools, runtime, and database when creating a project, the cloud destination may be largely decided much earlier.
Agents do not make every technical decision. Enterprise cost, security, compliance, and architecture still matter.
But defaults may matter more for lightweight and early-stage applications.
Astro and Vite integration gains new strategic significance.
Cloudflare is competing for software generated, built, and deployed by AI, not only serving existing developers.
Influencing creation is insufficient: applications must ultimately consume compute, storage, and networking on its platform.
That is Workers’ commercial role.
5. Workers as Infrastructure for AI Applications
Astro and Vite are not the main products Cloudflare ultimately sells.
Their value depends substantially on broadening Workers adoption and demand for paid services.
Consider an AI-generated web application.
It might start with Vite, build an Astro or other framework interface, and run backend logic on Workers.
D1 stores data, R2 files, Workflows long-running tasks, and Durable Objects real-time state.
Workers AI, AI Gateway, and other agent facilities can supply AI capabilities.
Cloudflare then offers an interconnected infrastructure set, rather than an isolated code execution environment.
During 2026 it also introduced capabilities including Dynamic Workers and Durable Object Facets.
Dynamic Workers load and execute code on demand, useful immediately after agents generate it. Facets let dynamically created applications use Durable Objects with isolated state and SQLite databases.
These capabilities deserve attention.
Coding platforms may host not only themselves but huge numbers of small user-generated applications.
Each may have little traffic, but the platform needs many code instances and secure user isolation.
Dedicated servers or containers per application can be costly.
V8 isolate density provides another option.
Isolates cannot run every workload. Agents needing full operating systems, arbitrary binaries, or complex native dependencies still need containers or other mechanisms.
Cloudflare is also developing Sandboxes for such cases.
Its strategy combines execution and storage capabilities around Workers rather than claiming Workers solves every compute requirement.
If AI dramatically increases software volume, especially small applications previously uneconomic to build, low-operations, automatically scaling infrastructure may find a larger market.
Technical possibility must nevertheless be separated from realized business results.
More generated software does not imply proportional paid-cloud revenue. Many applications may be temporary demos or attract no users.
Cloudflare must turn deployment interest into stable production workloads and paid consumption.
6. Deno/celld: How Self-Hosting Could Expand the Commercial Market
Astro and VoidZero promote tools and deployment workflows; celld strengthens Workers from another direction.
It asks whether adopting the Workers model requires staying on Cloudflare’s hosting.
This appears to conflict with commercial interests.
If customers run compatible compute on their own servers, demand for Cloudflare’s paid compute, storage, networking, and security might decline.
Workers principal designer Kenton Varda addressed this in October 2026.

He recalled that when Workers for Platforms was promoted to Shopify and other large customers in 2022, they required an open runtime. Enterprises hesitate to base core products on proprietary technology they cannot move.
Price changes, product shifts, or new terms could otherwise make migration exceptionally expensive.
Cloudflare open-sourced workerd in 2022 to reduce that concern.
It primarily handles code execution, however, without a mature multinode self-hosted Durable Objects system.
celld advances that direction.
Deno explored private-cluster execution with persistence and recovery built on SQLite, log replication, and object storage.
The integration plan makes this self-hosting capability an officially supported development direction for the Workers model.
The commercial logic differs from conventional lock-in.
Suppose an enterprise is choosing its platform for the next decade.
Option A is powerful but runs only on one provider’s infrastructure.
Option B offers similar development ergonomics and permits private deployment when necessary.
Even if the enterprise buys B’s hosted service, the option to move can increase adoption confidence.
Cloudflare seeks greater trust in Workers by reducing long-term lock-in risk.
Openness does not guarantee revenue growth.
Some customers may self-host and reduce purchases.
The bet is that portability attracts enough additional adoption to outweigh departures.
Integration remains ongoing. It has not turned the entire Cloudflare platform into self-hostable software.
Its global network, full ecosystem, enterprise operations, and security remain independently valuable.
Self-hosting compatible software and buying a hosted service also have different cost structures.
The goal may therefore be broadening the programming model itself, not one deployment method.
7. Cloudflare and Vercel: Converging Paths
Vercel is a constant presence as Cloudflare expands into development and deployment.
Closely associated with Next.js, it has long focused on web development and deployment experience.
While Cloudflare grew upward from networking and security, Vercel entered through frontend ergonomics, frameworks, and continuous deployment.
A team builds with Next.js, pushes to Git, and uses Vercel for builds, previews, and deployment.
That framework-to-hosting connection has been a major advantage.
AI is changing its product boundaries too.
v0 generates applications from natural language. AI SDK, AI Gateway, Sandbox, and Workflow SDK address model calls, routing, code execution, and durable workflows.
In 2026, Vercel explicitly positioned itself around agentic infrastructure.
It aims to support coding-agent deployments, enterprise agent development, and agents managing production systems, not just traditional web hosting.
In April 2026, it reported coding agents initiated over 30% of deployments. This is a statistic for Vercel’s own platform, not the industry, but demonstrates a material workflow impact.
The companies consequently compete in more areas.
Both seek AI-generated applications, provide agent environments, workflows, and cloud execution, and integrate development with deployment.
Their accumulated strengths differ:
Cloudflare brings networking, security, Workers, and distributed compute and data services.
Vercel brings web ergonomics, frameworks, deployment workflows, and a platform around AI SDK, v0, and Agent Stack.
That influences their competitive paths.
Cloudflare moves upward into frameworks and tools; Vercel moves downward into compute, storage, and agent execution.
This is a broad description, not a claim that Cloudflare lacks developer experience expertise or Vercel lacks infrastructure.
Both also emphasize openness. Next.js is not Vercel-exclusive, and Vercel introduced Bring Your Own Cloud for some enterprise scenarios in 2026. An open-versus-closed dichotomy would be misleading.
They compete for the tools and environments developers and agents choose when creating software.
8. What Determines Whether the Strategy Succeeds?
Together, the acquisitions build three related advantages.
Developer reach: Astro extends framework participation, while Vite reaches a wider range of JavaScript projects and workflows.
Integration: connecting Vite, workerd, Workers, D1, R2, and Durable Objects can simplify development, testing, deployment, and operation.
Portability: Deno/celld could reduce dependence on Cloudflare hosting and lower enterprises’ long-term adoption risks.
The commercial path is:
More developers and agents use the tools; more applications adopt compatible architectures; some buy Cloudflare hosting, storage, security, and networking.
Several uncertainties remain.
First, tool adoption is not cloud market share.
Vite and Astro remain cross-platform, allowing deployment to AWS, Vercel, Netlify, or others.
Influence over tooling does not control deployment destinations.
Second, integration is difficult.
Astro, Vite, workerd, and celld have different goals and architectures. A coherent experience requires sustained effort.
Undermining neutrality for commercial advantage would damage community trust.
Third, more AI applications do not mean proportionally more valuable production workloads.
Actual operating costs, database performance, state management, GPU inference requirements, and enterprise security and operations still determine competitiveness.
Whether generated applications attract sufficient users and spending remains a market question.
Finally, broader Workers adoption would not guarantee exclusive commercial returns.
Other providers can build services around open, portable technology too.
Cloudflare must keep demonstrating that its hosting offers more value than self-hosting or competing services.
Conclusion: Competing over How Software Is Produced
The three transactions point beyond simply expanding cloud services.
Astro brings Cloudflare closer to application creation.
VoidZero/Vite extends its participation in development, builds, and tests.
Deno/celld could carry the Workers model beyond its own infrastructure.
Meanwhile, databases, object storage, sandboxes, workflows, and inference extend what those applications can use at runtime.
The deals do not prove control over future software standards or establish the final AI-coding market structure.
They do reveal a strategic choice:
Cloudflare wants to join developer workflows before software is built and deployed, rather than being considered only afterward.
Cloud providers historically competed for existing enterprise compute needs.
Lower creation barriers may generate many applications that did not exist or were not worth building before.
Simple, reliable, inexpensive default environments may capture those new workloads first.
From Astro to Vite to Deno, Cloudflare is trying to connect that opportunity into a complete platform.
It seeks influence over not only where future software runs, but also how it is created.

text.text: Cloudflare Workers 在其整体业务中的战略位置。
Astro、VoidZero/Vite、Deno 三笔收购分别补齐什么。
Cloudflare 为什么愿意让 Workers 可以自托管。
Cloudflare 与 Vercel 的不同发展路线。
AI Coding 如何改变软件开发工具链和部署入口。
Cloudflare 是否正在推动 Workers 成为一种通用应用运行标准？
2026 年，Cloudflare 在不到十个月的时间里，连续完成了三笔值得关注的交易。
1 月 16 日，Astro Technology Company 加入 Cloudflare。这家公司开发了广泛使用的 Web 框架 Astro。
6 月 4 日，Vue.js 和 Vite 的创造者尤雨溪（Evan You）领导的 VoidZero 公司加入 Cloudflare。其技术版图包括 Vite、Vitest、Rolldown、Oxc、Vite+ 等 JavaScript 开发工具。
10 月 9 日，Node.js 创始人 Ryan Dahl 带领 Deno 团队加入 Cloudflare。双方宣布整合 workerd 和 celld，推动 Workers 与 Durable Objects 的自托管分布式运行。
这三笔交易的标的看似没有太大关联。
Astro 是 Web 应用框架，Vite 是开发与构建工具链，Deno 是 JavaScript 运行时及云计算平台，而 celld 则是一套分布式运行系统。
更奇怪的是，其中很多产品都不是 Cloudflare 独有的。Astro 和 Vite 本来就可以与其他云平台配合使用，celld 甚至让开发者有可能不使用 Cloudflare 的云服务器，也能运行采用 Workers 编程模型的应用。
一家靠提供云服务赚钱的公司，为什么要投入大量资源建设这些可以脱离自家平台使用的技术？
如果只从单笔收购来看，似乎很难解释。
但将三笔交易放在一起，再结合 Cloudflare 在 2026 年对 AI Agent、Workers 和开发者平台的持续投入，就能看到一条逐渐清晰的路线：
Cloudflare 正在从一个提供网络与计算基础设施的平台，向软件开发、构建、运行的整个生命周期扩张。
在 AI Coding 逐渐改变软件生产方式的背景下，这不只是一次产品线扩张，也可能意味着云计算公司的竞争重点正在发生变化。
一、Cloudflare 为什么需要向开发工具链扩张？
理解 Cloudflare 的战略，首先需要回到它原本的业务基础。
Cloudflare 早期主要提供 CDN、DNS、DDoS 防护、Web 应用防火墙等网络服务。它的核心优势，是遍布全球的网络基础设施，以及对大量互联网流量的处理能力。
随着业务发展，Cloudflare 逐渐从网站安全与加速，扩展到 Zero Trust 网络安全、网络连接、应用开发及计算服务等市场。
Workers 在这一转型过程中扮演了重要角色。
传统 CDN 主要负责缓存和传输内容，而 Workers 让开发者可以直接在 Cloudflare 的网络上执行应用程序。
这意味着 Cloudflare 不再只是帮助客户把已经开发好的应用交付给用户，而是开始参与应用本身的运行。
随后，Cloudflare 围绕 Workers 建立了 D1、R2、KV、Durable Objects、Queues、Workflows 等产品。
开发者可以使用 Workers 执行业务逻辑，通过 D1 保存结构化数据，使用 R2 存储文件，再利用 Durable Objects 管理实时状态。
到这一步，Cloudflare 已经开始具备一套完整后端平台的基本能力。
但问题随之出现：
拥有一套技术上可行的云平台，并不意味着开发者会优先选择它。
软件开发者在真正部署应用之前，往往已经做出了许多技术选择。
例如，使用什么框架创建网站，采用什么工具组织项目，如何构建和测试程序，选择哪一种运行时，以及怎样连接数据库与部署平台。
这些选择往往相互关联。
一个使用 Next.js 开发的团队，可能因为它与 Vercel 的深度集成，自然选择 Vercel 部署。一个使用特定云厂商数据库、消息队列和身份验证服务的应用，也可能因为迁移成本而继续留在原有平台。
这种竞争不是简单的服务器价格竞争，而是开发者工作流的竞争。
如果 Cloudflare 只在应用开发完成后才争取部署机会，就需要面对开发者此前已经形成的技术选择和使用习惯。
因此，它开始向软件开发链条的上游扩张。
Astro 和 VoidZero 的价值，正是在这个背景下变得清晰。
二、Astro：从云计算基础设施进入 Web 应用框架
2026 年 1 月，Cloudflare 宣布 Astro Technology Company 团队加入公司。
Astro 是一个主要面向内容驱动型网站的开源 Web 框架，广泛用于文档站点、博客、营销网站及其他内容型 Web 应用。
与强调客户端交互的某些前端框架不同，Astro 的设计十分注重服务器端生成 HTML、减少不必要的客户端 JavaScript，以及提升页面加载性能。
它采用 Islands Architecture（孤岛架构）等设计，让大部分页面以相对轻量的 HTML 呈现，只对需要交互的局部组件加载相应的客户端代码。
这种技术取向与 Cloudflare 原本的网络性能优势具有天然关联。
Cloudflare 已经擅长快速交付 Web 内容，而 Astro 擅长让开发者创建轻量、高性能的内容型网站。
但 Cloudflare 看中的显然不只是这一点。
Astro 同时也是一些应用生成平台和网站开发平台采用的技术基础。
Cloudflare 在收购公告中提到，基于其基础设施构建的 Webflow Cloud 和 Wix Vibe 等平台，已经采用 Astro 来创建和部署用户网站。
这意味着 Astro 的使用者不一定是传统意义上的专业前端开发者。
他们可能是通过某个 SaaS 平台生成网站的企业用户，也可能是在 AI 辅助下创建 Web 应用的人。
当这些平台使用 Astro 创建应用时，Astro 就进入了软件生产链条中非常靠前的位置。
Cloudflare 支持 Astro，可以改善框架与 Workers 平台之间的开发和部署体验，也能让更多使用 Astro 的开发者接触到自己的基础设施。
不过，不能因此认为 Cloudflare 准备将 Astro 变成只能运行在 Workers 上的专属框架。
恰恰相反，Cloudflare 明确承诺 Astro 继续保持开源、MIT 许可证和跨平台部署能力。
它仍然可以部署到其他云服务商，而不是被 Cloudflare 独占。
这反映了一种值得注意的策略：
Cloudflare 并不试图通过封闭框架强制获取用户，而是希望通过框架与自家云平台之间更顺畅的配合，提高开发者主动选择 Cloudflare 的概率。
Astro 因此成为 Cloudflare 向软件开发上游扩张的一个切入点。
但框架只是整个开发过程中的一部分。
相比单独支持一个 Web 框架，影响开发者使用的底层工具链，可能具有更加广泛的作用。
这就引出了 VoidZero。
三、VoidZero / Vite：争夺比单一框架更广泛的开发者入口
2026 年 6 月，Cloudflare 宣布 VoidZero 团队加入公司。
这笔交易的战略意义与 Astro 有明显区别。
Astro 是一种具体的 Web 框架，而 Vite 是服务于大量不同框架和应用的开发构建工具。
Vue、React、Svelte 等生态中的许多项目，都可以使用 Vite 作为开发服务器和构建基础。
Vite 解决的不是网站页面应该怎样设计，而是开发者怎样高效启动项目、编译模块、更新代码，以及生成可部署的程序。
VoidZero 进一步围绕 Vite 建立了一整套 JavaScript 工具链。
Vitest 负责测试，Rolldown 负责打包，Oxc、Oxlint、Oxfmt 分别提供解析、代码检查、格式化等相关能力，Vite+ 则试图将这些工具整合成更统一的开发体验。
这类工具对于软件开发的影响，远远超出了任何一个具体框架。
开发者可能不使用 Astro，也不使用 Vue，但只要开发过程依赖 Vite 及其相关工具，就可能与这套生态发生联系。
Cloudflare 因此获得了参与 JavaScript 基础工具链发展的机会。
更重要的是，Vite 与 Workers 之间已经存在实质性的技术合作。
早在 2024 年，Cloudflare 就与 Vite 团队合作设计 Environment API，使 Vite 在本地开发时可以支持 Node.js 以外的服务器运行环境。
Cloudflare 随后建立了官方 Vite 插件，将本地开发流程与 workerd 连接起来。
开发者可以在本地 Vite 开发服务器中执行 Workers 代码，调用 Durable Objects、D1 等能力，尽量减少本地与云端运行环境之间的差异。
这解决了一个长期存在的问题：本地开发环境与生产环境不一致。
过去，程序可能在本地 Node.js 环境中运行正常，部署到 Cloudflare Workers 后却因为 API 或运行时差异出现问题。
通过 Vite Environment API 和 Cloudflare 的运行时集成，开发者可以在本地获得更接近实际部署环境的体验。
但双方的合作并不止于此。
Cloudflare 在 2026 年的收购公告中明确提出，希望进一步将自己的应用工具链建立在 Vite 之上。
它正在探索的统一 CLI
cf
，目标是让
cf dev
cf build
cf deploy
与开发者熟悉的 Vite 工作流自然衔接。
这种思路与简单地把 Vite 改造成 Cloudflare 专属工具不同。
Cloudflare 明确承诺 Vite 继续保持供应商中立，其他云平台同样可以通过通用接口支持自己的运行时和部署方式。
Cloudflare 希望做的是：让自己的开发体验尽可能融入 Vite 生态，而不是要求开发者放弃 Vite 原有的开放性。
从商业角度看，这是一种更加间接的获客方式。
开发者选择 Vite，不意味着他们一定会选择 Cloudflare。
但当 Cloudflare 的开发、测试、部署体验与 Vite 深度结合时，部署到 Workers 就可能成为一条更自然、摩擦更小的技术路径。
而到了 AI Coding 时代，这种优势可能被进一步放大。
四、AI Coding 为什么让开发工具链的战略价值上升？
传统软件开发主要依靠人类程序员组织代码、配置环境、运行测试，再将应用部署到服务器上。
AI Coding 改变了其中一部分工作：越来越多程序不再由人从头逐行编写，而是由 AI Agent 生成项目结构、修改代码、安装依赖、启动开发服务器、执行测试，并根据错误信息反复修正程序。
在这种工作方式下，开发工具链的重要性可能进一步提高。
过去，开发者可能一天执行几十次构建或测试；现在，一个不断迭代的 Coding Agent，可以在短时间内重复执行大量开发操作。
工具越稳定、启动越快、错误信息越容易解析，Agent 完成任务的效率就可能越高。
Cloudflare 在收购 VoidZero 的公告中，特别强调了这一变化：
Vite、Vitest、Rolldown、Oxlint 等工具的高速执行和可组合能力，不仅服务于人类开发者，也适合 AI Agent 频繁运行。
但 AI 带来的变化并不局限于工具调用次数增加。
一个更值得关注的变化是：
软件生产、部署和运行之间的边界正在缩短。
传统开发通常存在相对清晰的阶段：需求分析、编码、测试、构建、部署、运维。
而在 AI Coding 平台中，用户可能只需要输入一句自然语言需求，系统便自动生成应用、启动预览、运行测试，最后完成部署。
开发与部署不再是两个完全独立的流程，而逐渐融入同一个交互过程。
这也改变了云厂商获取开发者的时机。
过去，云平台主要在程序开发完成后争取部署需求。
现在，如果某个 AI Coding 平台在创建项目时，就已经默认选择框架、工具链、运行时和数据库，那么最终使用哪家云平台，可能在开发初期就基本确定。
这并不意味着 AI Agent 已经取代开发者做出所有技术决策。企业的成本、安全、合规和架构要求仍然重要。
但对大量轻量级应用和早期项目来说，开发工具的默认配置可能正在变得更加重要。
Cloudflare 整合 Astro 与 Vite，也就具有了新的战略意义。
它不仅是在服务现有开发者，更是在争取那些通过 AI 自动生成、构建和部署的软件。
不过，影响软件如何被创建还不够。Cloudflare 最终还是需要让这些应用运行在自己的平台上，形成实际的计算、存储和网络服务需求。
这就是 Workers 的商业位置。
五、Cloudflare 想让 Workers 成为 AI 应用的运行基础
从商业模式上看，Astro 和 Vite 并不是 Cloudflare 最终要出售的主要商品。
这些开放开发工具的价值，很大程度上体现在它们能否扩大 Workers 生态，以及能否让更多应用使用 Cloudflare 的付费服务。
考虑一个由 AI Agent 自动生成的 Web 应用。
它可能首先使用 Vite 创建项目，采用 Astro 或其他框架生成界面，再使用 Workers 运行后端逻辑。
如果需要保存数据，可以接入 D1；如果需要保存文件，可以使用 R2；如果需要长期运行的任务，可以使用 Workflows；如果需要实时状态管理，则可以使用 Durable Objects。
如果这个应用本身还包含 AI 能力，Cloudflare 还提供 Workers AI、AI Gateway，以及其他 Agent 开发与执行设施。
这样一来，Cloudflare 能够提供的不再是一个孤立的代码执行环境，而是应用运行过程中需要的一整组基础设施。
2026 年，Cloudflare 又推出了 Dynamic Workers、Durable Object Facets 等能力。
前者允许平台动态加载和运行代码，适合 AI Agent 生成代码后立即执行等场景；后者则使动态创建的应用能够使用具有隔离状态和 SQLite 数据库的 Durable Objects。
这类产品尤其值得关注。
因为 AI Coding 平台不只需要托管自己的应用，还可能需要托管用户通过 AI 创建的海量小型应用。
每个应用可能访问量很低，但整个应用平台需要支持极大量的代码实例，并保障不同用户之间的安全隔离。
传统为每个应用分配独立服务器或容器的方式，可能带来较大的运行成本。
Cloudflare 基于 V8 Isolate 的高密度计算模型，则为这种应用形态提供了另一种选择。
当然，Isolate 并非可以承担任何类型的计算。对于需要完整操作系统环境、任意二进制程序或复杂本地依赖的 Agent，仍然需要容器或其他计算机制。
Cloudflare 也在发展 Sandboxes 等产品，以覆盖这类场景。
因此，Cloudflare 的实际路线并不是用 Workers 解决全部计算需求，而是围绕 Workers 建立一套能够组合不同执行与存储能力的平台。
如果 AI 使软件数量大幅增长，尤其催生大量过去不值得专门开发的小型应用，那么这种低运维成本、可自动扩缩容的基础设施可能获得新的市场空间。
但这里必须区分技术可能性与已经实现的商业结果。
更多软件被生成，不必然意味着同等比例的付费云收入增长。很多生成的应用可能只是短期演示项目，或者根本没有实际用户。
Cloudflare 最终仍需证明，它不仅能够吸引应用部署，还能够让这些应用形成稳定的生产负载和商业消费。
六、Deno / celld：为什么开放自托管能力，反而可能扩大商业市场？
如果说 Astro 与 VoidZero 主要推动开发者采用 Cloudflare 的工具和部署工作流，那么 Deno 团队带来的 celld，则从另一个方向补强了 Workers 生态。
它解决的是应用采用 Workers 编程模型之后，能否脱离 Cloudflare 自家的托管环境运行。
这个问题表面上与 Cloudflare 的商业利益存在冲突。
Cloudflare 依靠提供计算、存储、网络和安全服务收费。假如开发者能够在自己的服务器上运行 Workers 和 Durable Objects，岂不是减少了对 Cloudflare 的依赖？
Cloudflare Workers 核心设计者 Kenton Varda 在 2026 年 10 月的公告中，直接回应了这一问题。
他回忆，2022 年 Cloudflare 向 Shopify 等大型客户推广 Workers for Platforms 时，客户提出的重要条件之一，就是 Workers 底层运行时必须开源：
大型企业往往不愿意将核心业务建立在一套完全无法迁移的专有技术之上。
因为一旦云厂商改变价格、产品方向或者服务条款，客户可能需要付出极高的迁移成本。
为了消除这种顾虑，Cloudflare 在 2022 年开源了 workerd。
但 workerd 主要解决了代码执行问题，对于在多台服务器上自托管 Durable Objects，仍然缺少一套成熟的分布式实现。
celld 则沿着这个方向更进一步。
Deno 团队探索了如何让 Workers 和 Durable Objects 的应用，在开发者自己的服务器集群中运行，并通过 SQLite、日志复制与对象存储实现持久化和故障恢复。
Cloudflare 与 Deno 宣布的整合计划，就是让这种自托管能力成为 Workers 编程模型正式支持的发展方向。
这背后是一种与传统厂商锁定不同的商业逻辑。
假设一家大型企业正在选择未来十年的应用开发平台。
方案 A 的技术能力很强，但只能在某一家云服务商的基础设施上运行。
方案 B 则提供类似的开发体验，并允许企业在必要时部署到自己的服务器上。
即使企业最终仍然选择使用方案 B 的付费托管服务，拥有迁移选择权本身，也可能提高它采用这套技术的意愿。
换句话说，
Cloudflare 试图用降低厂商锁定风险的方式，换取更多企业对 Workers 编程模型的信任。
这并不意味着开源与开放必然带来更多收入。
部分客户确实可能选择自行部署，从而减少购买 Cloudflare 托管服务的需求。
Cloudflare 赌的是，
因可移植性而愿意采用 Workers 的新增客户，最终能够带来比客户迁出更大的商业价值。
但需要强调，celld 与 workerd 的整合目前仍然是持续推进的工程，并没有使整个 Cloudflare 云平台变成可以完整自托管的软件。
Cloudflare 的全球网络、完整产品生态、企业级运维与安全服务，依然具有独立价值。
对企业而言，自己运行一套兼容 Workers 的系统，与购买 Cloudflare 的托管服务，也仍然是两种不同的成本结构。
所以，Cloudflare 真正想扩大的可能不是某一种部署方式，而是 Workers 编程模型本身的适用范围。
七、Cloudflare 与 Vercel：两条路线正在交汇
当 Cloudflare 在应用开发部署领域持续攻城略地时，Vercel 总是如影随形。
Vercel 与 Next.js 生态联系紧密，长期专注于改善 Web 应用开发与部署体验。
相比 Cloudflare 从 CDN、网络和安全基础设施向上发展，Vercel 更早从前端开发者体验、Web 框架和持续部署流程切入市场。
开发者使用 Next.js 创建项目，再将代码提交到 Git 仓库，通过 Vercel 完成构建、预览与部署。
这种从框架到托管平台的衔接，一直是 Vercel 的重要优势。
但进入 AI 时代，Vercel 也在改变自己的产品边界。
其 v0 允许用户通过自然语言生成应用；AI SDK、AI Gateway、Sandbox、Workflow SDK 等产品，则分别服务于模型调用、模型路由、代码执行与持久化工作流等需求。
2026 年，Vercel 明确提出 Agentic Infrastructure（智能体基础设施）的战略定位。
它不再满足于托管传统 Web 应用，而是希望成为 Coding Agent 部署软件、企业构建 Agent，以及平台自身利用 Agent 自动管理生产系统的基础设施。
Vercel 在 2026 年 4 月披露，彼时已有超过 30% 的平台部署由 Coding Agent 发起。这是 Vercel 自有平台的统计数据，并不代表整个行业的比例，但足以说明 AI Coding 对其业务流程已经产生实质性影响。
Cloudflare 和 Vercel 因此开始在越来越多的领域直接交锋。
两家公司都希望承载 AI 生成的应用，都在提供 Agent 运行环境、持久化工作流和云端代码执行能力，也都在尝试将开发与部署体验整合起来。
但两者仍然有不同的技术积累：
Cloudflare 的基础是全球网络、安全系统、Workers 运行时，以及大量分布式计算与数据服务。
Vercel 的基础则是 Web 开发体验、框架生态、应用部署流程，以及围绕 AI SDK、v0 和 Agent Stack 建立的开发平台。
这种差异也影响它们各自的竞争路线。
Cloudflare 从基础设施向上进入框架和开发工具链；Vercel 从框架与开发者体验向下扩展计算、存储和 Agent 运行平台。
当然，这只是对双方发展路径的概括，并不意味着 Cloudflare 不擅长开发者体验，或者 Vercel 缺乏基础设施技术。
两家公司也都强调开放性。Next.js 并不是只能部署在 Vercel，Vercel 在 2026 年还推出了面向部分企业场景的 Bring Your Own Cloud 能力。因此，不能简单地将两者描述为「开放平台」与「封闭平台」的对立。
它们真正争夺的，是开发者和 AI Agent 在创建软件时，最终选择哪一套工具与运行环境。
八、Cloudflare 的战略能否成功，取决于什么？
把 Astro、VoidZero 和 Deno 放在一起，可以看到 Cloudflare 正在建立三个相互联系的优势。
首先是开发者触达能力：Astro 帮助 Cloudflare 更深入地参与 Web 框架生态，Vite 则让它能够接触更加广泛的 JavaScript 项目与开发流程。
其次是平台整合能力：通过让 Vite、workerd、Workers、D1、R2、Durable Objects 等产品更加紧密地协同，Cloudflare 希望降低开发、测试、部署以及运行应用的复杂度。
最后是编程模型的可移植性：Deno / celld 带来的技术，有望让 Workers 不再完全依赖 Cloudflare 的托管基础设施，从而降低部分企业采用这一编程模型时的长期风险。
三者共同构成了一条商业路径：
更多开发者和 AI Agent 使用相关工具，更多应用采用兼容 Workers 的架构，其中一部分最终选择 Cloudflare 提供的托管计算、存储、安全和网络服务。
但这条路径中仍然存在几个不确定性。
首先，开放工具的普及不等于 Cloudflare 的市场份额增长。
Vite 和 Astro 都承诺保持跨平台兼容，开发者可以使用这些工具，同时选择 AWS、Vercel、Netlify 或其他云服务商。
Cloudflare 能够影响工具链的发展，却不代表能够控制这些工具的用户最终部署到哪里。
其次，技术整合本身并不简单。
Astro、Vite、workerd、celld 原本具有不同的研发目标和技术架构。将它们组织成一致的开发体验，需要长期投入。
如果为了强调 Cloudflare 自家的商业利益而损害工具的供应商中立性，会强烈降低开发者社区对项目的信任感。
再次，AI 应用数量的增长不等于高质量生产负载的同比例增长。
应用运行的真实成本、数据库访问性能、状态管理能力、GPU 推理需求，以及企业级安全和运维保障，依然决定着云平台的长期竞争力。
而且，AI Agent 生成的应用虽然可能数量庞大，但是否具有足够的用户规模和付费能力，仍然需要市场验证。
最后，即便 Workers 编程模型获得更广泛的认可，Cloudflare 也未必能够独占这种生态的商业收益。
当某种技术变得开放和可移植时，其他企业同样可能围绕它提供服务。
因此，Cloudflare 在推动模型普及的同时，还必须持续证明自己的托管平台比自行部署和其他竞争服务更有价值。
结语：争夺的不只是云计算资源，而是软件的生产方式
回顾 Cloudflare 在 2026 年的三笔交易，可以发现它们共同指向了一个比单纯扩大云计算业务更复杂的目标。
Astro 让 Cloudflare 更接近应用创建过程。
VoidZero / Vite 让 Cloudflare 深入开发、构建和测试环节。
Deno / celld 则让 Workers 编程模型有机会跨越 Cloudflare 自家的基础设施，成为可以在更多环境中运行的计算方式。
与此同时，Cloudflare 继续围绕 Workers 扩展数据库、对象存储、代码沙箱、持久化工作流和 AI 推理等能力，希望为这些应用提供实际运行所需的基础设施。
这三笔交易不能证明 Cloudflare 已经掌握了未来的软件开发标准，也不能说明 AI Coding 时代的市场格局已经确定。
但它们表明了一种明确的战略选择：
Cloudflare 不再满足于成为软件开发完成后才被考虑的基础设施供应商，而是希望在软件被创建、构建、部署之前，就已经成为开发者工作流的一部分。
过去，云厂商主要争夺的是企业已有的计算需求。
而 AI Coding 可能使软件的生产门槛下降，创造出大量过去不存在、或者不值得专门开发的新应用。
在这样的市场中，谁能够提供简单、稳定、低成本的默认开发与运行环境，谁就可能率先接触到这些新增的计算需求。
从 Astro 到 Vite，再到 Deno，Cloudflare 正在尝试把这一机会连接成一套完整的平台能力。
它想争取的，不只是未来的软件在哪里运行，还包括未来的软件将以什么方式被创造出来。
