en.title: Why Did Deno Build celld? Cloudflare Workers Moves from a Cloud Service Toward an Open Execution Platform
en.subtitle: From Deno Deploy and Deno KV to celld: stateful distributed computing and convergence with Cloudflare Workers

text.text: Deno’s origins and the development of Deno Runtime and Deno Deploy.
Why Deno began exploring stateful distributed computing.
The origins of celld and its relationship to Durable Objects.
How SQLite, LTX, and object storage support celld’s distributed deployment.
Why celld is needed even though workerd is open source.
Why Cloudflare’s acquisition of Deno brings their technical paths together.
On October 9, 2026, Cloudflare announced that the Deno team was joining the company and that Deno’s celld would be integrated with Cloudflare’s workerd.
The news initially seemed surprising.

Deno founder Ryan Dahl created Node.js. He started Deno in 2018 to rethink JavaScript server runtimes. Deno subsequently developed both its runtime and Deno Deploy, a cloud platform competing directly with Cloudflare Workers.

Yet in August 2026, Deno released celld, an open-source project that implemented compatibility with Workers and Durable Objects rather than promoting its own application interfaces, allowing those programs to run on developers’ own servers.
Just two months later, the teams announced they were joining forces.
Why did a company challenging Cloudflare begin implementing its rival’s technology? What did celld offer beyond the already-open-source workerd? Why ultimately develop one system together?
This is more than an acquisition story. It reflects how Ryan Dahl’s decade-plus exploration of server programming models converged with Cloudflare’s approach.
1. From Node.js to Deno: Searching for Better Server Programming
Understanding celld begins with Ryan Dahl’s technical ambitions.
In 2009, he released Node.js, expanding JavaScript beyond its predominantly browser-based role.
An important design choice combined an event loop and asynchronous I/O so one JavaScript process could efficiently handle many concurrent network connections.

Servers previously often used multiple threads or processes for concurrency. Node.js did not invent asynchronous I/O, but combined it with JavaScript’s event-driven programming to make highly concurrent network services relatively simple to write.
Dahl’s initial Node.js demonstration was an IRC chat server of roughly 500 lines.
That example later became a source of reflection.
One server can handle many connections asynchronously, but further growth eventually requires multiple machines.
Consider 100,000 IRC users across 1,000 channels. One machine ultimately has limits in compute, memory, and bandwidth.
Distributing users across servers creates new problems: members of one channel may connect to different machines, requiring coordination of membership, messages, and live connection state.
Node.js simplified asynchronous networking on one machine without fundamentally simplifying distributed application design across machines.
In 2018, Dahl started Deno.
Its aim was a more modern, secure, and usable runtime for JavaScript and TypeScript.
Compared with Node.js, Deno emphasized permissions restricted by default, web-standard APIs, built-in TypeScript support, and integrated formatting, testing, and linting.
It sought to reduce environment and tooling configuration and make running JavaScript simpler.
In retrospect, these improvements primarily concerned the experience of writing and running programs.
Deploying a large internet application still involved servers, databases, storage, load balancing, and distributed coordination.
The team therefore expanded from a runtime into a cloud platform.
2. Deno Deploy: From Running JavaScript to Operating Distributed Applications
Deno Deploy released its first public beta in June 2021.
This was a significant move from developer tools into cloud services.

Deno Deploy is a serverless hosting platform for JavaScript, TypeScript, and WebAssembly. Developers deploy programs across geographic regions while the platform manages compute resources and requests.
Its positioning resembles Workers: developers submit code and the platform runs and scales it.
It is not built on Workers, however. Deno developed its own multitenant JavaScript execution platform from scratch.
For Dahl, this meant moving from runtime design to operating cloud infrastructure himself.
As Deploy evolved, the team recognized that running code on many servers did not necessarily make distributed applications easy to build.
The hardest part was often data.
Compute distributed globally still makes cross-region trips if the database remains centralized.
Moving compute closer to users does not necessarily make the whole application faster.
Database configuration, authentication, state synchronization, and recovery also do not disappear simply because execution is serverless.
Deno introduced Deno KV in May 2023 to address these concerns.

Deno KV is a key-value database closely integrated with the runtime. Simple JavaScript APIs let developers persist and read data without first installing, configuring, and connecting a separate database.
Locally it can use SQLite. Deno Deploy’s hosted implementation at the time used distributed storage based on FoundationDB.
Developers could manage persistent data locally and in the cloud through similar APIs.
KV simplified storage without solving everything.
A multiplayer game room must do more than store player records: it continuously processes actions, coordinates game state, manages connections, and broadcasts events.
A database can persist state without providing all of that room’s running logic.
Developers must still combine the systems if compute and state management remain separate.
In a May 2025 response to debate over Deno’s progress, Dahl acknowledged that KV had not adequately brought compute and state together.
He also disclosed a new project inspired by Cloudflare Durable Objects.
That was the key turning point.
Deno began asking not merely how to make databases easier, but whether compute, state, and distributed scaling could share one programming abstraction.
3. Why Cloudflare Durable Objects?
Durable Objects provide a different model from conventional stateless serverless execution.
Developers create uniquely identified business objects, each with execution logic and persistent storage. The platform manages placement, lifecycle, and routing.
A chat system can create one Durable Object per channel.
Channels A and B each get an object managing their members, messages, connections, and state changes.
As usage grows, different channels can execute on different servers.
Compute and data are partitioned by business object from the outset, rather than splitting a large application across machines only after traffic grows.
In October 2026, Dahl recalled that recognizing this model’s value brought him back to his original Node.js IRC server.
One object per channel makes each channel an independent distributed-system unit.
It has its own logic, SQLite database, and WebSocket connection management.
Adding channels adds independent objects that can be placed on more servers.
A single channel still has capacity limits, but different channels can scale horizontally with relative independence.
Dahl valued that distribution was considered in the programming model itself, rather than entirely bolted on after application development.
This explains Deno’s decision to support Cloudflare’s interfaces.
Its goal was not another JavaScript syntax, but easier development and operation of distributed applications.
Durable Objects already provided a relatively mature abstraction for that problem.
Adopting the model did not require using only Cloudflare’s hosted service.
AWS S3 offers an important analogy.
S3 began as an AWS product, but many other storage systems implemented its API. Developers can use similar interfaces across providers without always running on AWS.
Deno applied that idea to Durable Objects: keep the developer interface and reimplement execution, scheduling, and persistent storage.
That led to celld.
4. celld: Moving Durable Objects Beyond One Cloud
Dahl released celld on August 5, 2026, under Apache 2.0.
Its most direct description is:
Self-hosted, distributed Durable Objects.
Its value requires distinguishing what Cloudflare had already open-sourced from what remained outside a complete open deployment.
Cloudflare open-sourced the underlying Workers runtime, workerd, in September 2022.
Developers can run it locally or on their own servers to execute JavaScript following the Workers programming model.
But workerd is not the whole Cloudflare cloud platform.
Suppose a company has 100 servers for a multiplayer chat application using Durable Objects.
Installing workerd does not automatically produce the hosted platform’s distributed system.
It must still answer several questions:
Which server runs a particular chat-room object?
How does a user’s request reach that server?
If it crashes, how do other servers recover the room’s data and take over?
How do we prevent two servers both believing they may modify the same object?
Cloudflare’s infrastructure handles these in the hosted product.
At the time, open-source workerd primarily supported single-instance Durable Objects, not a complete self-hostable multinode execution system.
celld fills that gap.
It provides an independent execution system, not a plugin installed on Cloudflare’s servers.
Developers retain Workers and Durable Objects APIs while deploying on their own VMs or clusters.
celld executes code, assigns object ownership, routes requests, persists data, and recovers objects after failures.
Its question extends from running one object to reliably operating thousands across multiple servers.
5. celld’s Design: V8, SQLite, LTX, and Object Storage
The architecture is particularly interesting.
Distributed platforms often need databases, cluster coordinators, service discovery, schedulers, and failure detectors.
Even mature components add deployment and maintenance complexity.
Dahl wanted a simpler system: one executable plus shared object storage forming a distributed cluster.
It uses V8 for JavaScript, SQLite for each object’s data, LTX for replicating database changes, and S3-compatible or similar object storage for persistence and coordination.
Three design choices are central.
5.1 Each Cell Has Its Own SQLite Database
A Cell is a uniquely identified stateful compute unit corresponding to the basic Durable Object model.
It has its own logic and SQLite database.
Chat rooms A, B, and C each have a Cell. Their data is naturally partitioned by room, rather than packed into one global SQLite database.
Different Cells can execute on different servers.
This provides natural sharding: data is organized around independent business objects from the beginning, rather than partitioned only after a database grows large.
5.2 Object Storage Coordinates Ownership
This is among celld’s most distinctive choices.
Suppose server A runs room 001 and server B is available as a backup.
celld records ownership of room 001 in shared object storage.
Servers compete for execution ownership through conditional writes supported by the store.
Once A acquires ownership, B cannot simultaneously acquire valid ownership of the same object.
This requires sufficiently strong storage consistency and atomic conditional updates, together with leases, epochs, and similar mechanisms to fence off previous owners.
If A fails, another server can acquire ownership once takeover conditions are met.
celld avoids maintaining a separate cluster-membership and distributed-consensus service itself.
It does not eliminate distributed coordination. It builds part of that work on reliable primitives already supplied by object storage.
The underlying store therefore has explicit requirements. Not every product claiming S3 compatibility is safe for this use.
5.3 Replicating SQLite Through LTX
After ownership is resolved, acknowledged data must survive server failure.
celld records durable SQLite changes in LTX.
LTX is a SQLite replication log format related to Ben Johnson’s Litestream technology.
When a Cell’s database changes, celld can replicate changes to other nodes and continuously upload them to shared object storage.
In a multinode deployment, writes can meet the required durability conditions on other nodes’ disks before being acknowledged, with uploads to object storage following asynchronously.
This avoids waiting for an object-storage round trip on every write and can reduce storage operation costs.
After failure, a takeover node recovers acknowledged state from shared storage and any necessary node logs, then restarts the Cell.
One goal is zero loss of acknowledged writes, or RPO=0, within the specified failure model and deployment conditions.
That guarantee depends on storage reliability, replication configuration, and failure assumptions. It does not promise immunity to every hardware or network disaster.

The deployment model combines these capabilities: developers write Workers/Durable Objects code, operators run multiple celld instances connected to shared object storage, and the system manages ownership, replication, and failover.
This reduces separately maintained infrastructure components.
Self-hosting still requires managing capacity, networking, security, monitoring, and storage costs. It is not an operations-free hosted serverless service.
celld also remains a work in progress. Even with some surrounding Workers capabilities implemented, it is not a complete replacement for Cloudflare’s platform.
6. From Competition to Convergence: Why Deno Joined Cloudflare
The two technical paths had developed a complementary relationship.
Cloudflare had a widely adopted Workers model, a mature hosting platform, and the open-source workerd runtime.
Deno’s celld explored distributed Durable Objects outside Cloudflare with fewer infrastructure components.
One had a mature programming model and cloud; the other offered a new self-hosted distributed implementation.
They complemented different parts of one model rather than duplicating exactly the same work.
On October 9, 2026, Dahl and Workers principal designer Kenton Varda jointly announced that Deno would join Cloudflare and integrate celld with workerd.
The intention was not to replace workerd with Deno Runtime.
Both were independent JavaScript runtimes. Cloudflare did not need to abandon its own to gain celld’s distributed capabilities.
The aim was to combine workerd’s execution with celld’s cross-server scheduling, replication, and recovery.
The same Workers/Durable Objects model could then serve Cloudflare’s hosted network and customers’ own infrastructure.
This also required reallocating Deno’s development resources.

Dahl announced one year of monthly maintenance updates for Deno Runtime before the original team stopped developing it. Deno Deploy would close after six months, with paying customers helped to migrate to Workers.
The runtime would remain open source, and JSR was expected to continue operating with its infrastructure moved to Cloudflare.
This was a major trade-off.
Deno began as a Node.js challenger, and Deploy was a commercial product built over years.
The team now chose to invest its main future effort in another company’s model and platform.
Dahl’s account frames this not as abandoning the original ambition, but as finding a more important problem than improving one runtime.
Node.js reduced asynchronous networking complexity.
Deno sought to simplify JavaScript development and execution environments.
Deploy sought to simplify deployment.
celld seeks to distribute compute and coordinate state across servers without every team constructing complex distributed infrastructure itself.

On this path, Durable Objects are attractive because they compress complex distributed capabilities into a relatively simple abstraction, rather than merely adding another infrastructure component to learn.
7. Why Would Cloudflare Open Its Technology?
Competitively, celld could have threatened Cloudflare.
Self-hosting compatible applications could reduce the need to buy its compute services.
Cloudflare offered a different business interpretation.
In the joint announcement, Varda argued that making Workers applications difficult to move was not an advantage worth pursuing.
For some large enterprises, inability to migrate is precisely a reason not to adopt a technology.
He recalled that customers including Shopify required an open-source runtime when Workers for Platforms was promoted in 2022, before entrusting core products to it.
Cloudflare subsequently open-sourced workerd.
Varda said some customers had indeed used it to leave Cloudflare, but portability also persuaded more enterprises to adopt Workers initially.
celld takes that direction further.
Durable Objects can become a programming model implementable on other infrastructure, not merely a hosted Cloudflare service.
A genuinely universal cross-provider standard is still some distance away.

API coverage, runtime behavior, availability guarantees, and operational maturity need further development. Applications deeply dependent on Cloudflare’s services cannot assume they can move unchanged today.
The announcement establishes an integration direction, not an already complete, fully compatible open platform.
The important point is the companies’ converging view of future server applications.
Developers may need more than faster runtimes or cheaper compute: a model making distributed computing and state management easier to use.
Deno has evolved from a Node.js challenger into a proponent of that model.
Cloudflare aims to keep providing hosted compute while broadening infrastructure support for Workers and Durable Objects.
celld is therefore neither a next-generation replacement for Durable Objects nor an ordinary Deno add-on to Cloudflare products.
It is an attempt to turn stateful serverless capabilities originally supplied by one cloud provider into a software execution model available on different infrastructure.

Afterword: why Cloudflare would invest in making its hosting easier to leave, and why it brought together Astro, VoidZero/Vite, and Deno during 2026, reaches beyond runtime technology. These decisions form part of a broader strategy around development toolchains, developer entry points, and the cloud market in the AI era.

en.excerpt: Deno’s origins and the development of Deno Runtime and Deno Deploy.  Why Deno began exploring stateful distributed computing.  The origins of celld and its relationship to Durable

text.text: Deno 的起源，以及 Deno Runtime、Deno Deploy 的发展。
Deno 为什么开始探索有状态分布式计算。
celld 的诞生及其与 Durable Objects 的关系。
celld 如何通过 SQLite、LTX、对象存储等实现分布式部署。
workerd 已经开源，为什么仍然需要 celld？
Cloudflare 收购 Deno，双方技术路线为何最终汇合？
2026 年 10 月 9 日，Cloudflare 宣布 Deno 团队正式加入公司，并将 Deno 开发的 celld 与 Cloudflare 的 workerd 进行整合。
这一消息看起来有些出人意料。
Deno 的创始人 Ryan Dahl 是 Node.js 的创造者。2018 年，他启动 Deno 项目，希望重新设计 JavaScript 的服务器运行时。此后，Deno 不仅推出了自己的运行时，还建立了 Deno Deploy 云计算平台，与 Cloudflare Workers 形成直接竞争。
然而，2026 年 8 月，Deno 团队却发布了一个名叫 celld 的开源项目。它不再尝试推广一套属于 Deno 自己的应用接口，而是直接兼容 Cloudflare Workers 和 Durable Objects，让开发者能够在自己的服务器上运行这类程序。
仅仅两个月后，两支团队就宣布合流。
为什么一家原本挑战 Cloudflare 的公司，反而开始实现对手的技术？既然 Cloudflare 已经将 workerd 开源，celld 又有什么独特价值？两家公司最后为什么决定共同开发同一套系统？
这件事情的关键，并不只是一次企业收购，而是 Ryan Dahl 十余年来对服务器编程模型的探索，最终与 Cloudflare 的技术路线走到了一起。
一、从 Node.js 到 Deno：Ryan Dahl 一直在寻找更好的服务器编程方式
要理解 celld 的诞生，首先需要理解 Ryan Dahl 的技术追求。
2009 年，Ryan Dahl 发布了 Node.js，改变了 JavaScript 主要运行在浏览器中的局面。
Node.js 的一个重要设计，是利用事件循环和异步 I/O，使单个 JavaScript 进程能够高效处理大量并发网络连接。
在此之前，服务器程序通常依靠多线程、多进程等方式管理并发连接。异步 I/O 并非 Node.js 首创，但 Node.js 将这一机制与 JavaScript 的事件驱动编程结合起来，使开发者能够用相对简单的方式编写高并发网络服务。
Ryan Dahl 在最初展示 Node.js 时，使用的就是一个只有约 500 行代码的 IRC 聊天服务器。
但这个例子后来也成为他反思的问题。
单台服务器可以通过异步 I/O 同时处理大量连接，可当用户数量继续增长，系统仍然需要扩展到多台机器。
例如，一个 IRC 聊天系统拥有十万个用户，分布在一千个频道中。单台服务器终究存在计算、内存和网络带宽的上限。
如果把用户分配到多台服务器，新的问题就出现了：同一个频道的用户可能连接不同服务器，频道成员、消息和实时连接状态需要在服务器之间协调。
Node.js 简化了单台服务器上的异步网络编程，却没有从根本上简化跨服务器的分布式应用设计。
2018 年，Ryan Dahl 启动 Deno 项目。
Deno 的目标，是重新设计一个更加现代、安全、易用的 JavaScript 和 TypeScript 运行时。
相比 Node.js，Deno 强调默认权限限制、Web 标准 API、原生 TypeScript 支持，以及内置格式化、测试、代码检查等开发工具。
它试图减少开发者需要自行配置的工具和环境，让运行 JavaScript 程序变得更加简单。
但从后来的发展看，Deno 主要改善的仍然是编写和运行 JavaScript 程序的体验。
如果开发者需要部署一个大规模互联网应用，依然要面对服务器、数据库、存储、负载均衡和分布式协调等基础设施问题。
于是，Deno 团队开始从运行时向云计算平台扩展。
二、Deno Deploy：从运行 JavaScript，到运营分布式应用
2021 年 6 月，Deno Deploy 发布首个公开测试版本。
这是 Deno 从开发工具向云计算服务迈出的重要一步。
Deno Deploy 是一个面向 JavaScript、TypeScript 和 WebAssembly 的 Serverless 托管平台，允许开发者将程序部署到多个地理位置的服务器上，由平台负责计算资源和请求处理。
它与 Cloudflare Workers 有相似的产品定位：开发者提交代码，云平台负责运行和扩容。
但 Deno Deploy 并不是建立在 Cloudflare Workers 之上的服务。Deno 团队从头开发了自己的多租户 JavaScript 执行平台。
对 Ryan Dahl 来说，这也是
从设计运行时转向亲自运营云计算基础设施的过程。
然而，随着 Deno Deploy 的发展，团队逐渐意识到：让代码在很多台服务器上运行，并不等于让分布式应用变得容易开发。
真正复杂的地方往往是数据。
如果计算实例部署在全球多个地区，而数据库仍然集中在某一个数据中心，应用依然需要不断跨区域访问数据库。
计算越接近用户，并不一定意味着整个应用响应越快。
同时，数据库配置、身份验证、状态同步和故障恢复等工作，也没有因为使用了 Serverless 就自然消失。
为了解决这些问题，Deno 在 2023 年 5 月推出了 Deno KV。
Deno KV 是一个与 Deno 运行时深度集成的键值数据库。开发者可以通过简单的 JavaScript API 保存和读取数据，不必首先安装、配置和连接一套独立的数据库系统。
在本地环境中，Deno KV 可以使用 SQLite；在当时的 Deno Deploy 托管环境中，则使用基于 FoundationDB 的分布式存储架构。
这让开发者能够使用相近的 API，在本地和云端管理持久化数据。
Deno KV 确实简化了应用的数据存储问题，但它没有解决所有问题。
例如，一个多人游戏房间不仅需要保存玩家数据，还需要持续处理玩家动作、协调游戏状态、管理网络连接，并向其他玩家广播事件。
数据库可以保存状态，却不能直接承担这个房间全部的运行逻辑。
如果计算与状态管理仍然分属不同的系统，开发者就需要自行组合它们。
2025 年 5 月，Ryan Dahl 在一篇回应 Deno 发展争议的文章中，公开承认 Deno KV 没有充分解决计算与状态紧密结合的问题。
他同时明确透露，团队正在开发一个新项目，其设计受到了 Cloudflare Durable Objects 的启发。
这是整个故事最重要的转折点。
Deno 不再只是试图把数据库做得更容易使用，而是开始重新思考：
能不能把应用的计算、状态和分布式扩展组织为同一种编程抽象？
三、为什么偏偏选择 Cloudflare 的 Durable Objects？
Cloudflare 的 Durable Objects 提供了一个与传统无状态 Serverless 不同的模型。
它让开发者能够创建具有唯一身份的业务对象。每个对象有自己的执行逻辑和持久存储，并由平台负责管理对象的运行位置、生命周期和请求路由。
对于多人聊天系统，可以为每个频道创建一个 Durable Object。
频道 A 有自己的对象，频道 B 有自己的对象。每个对象负责对应频道的成员、消息、网络连接和状态变化。
当系统规模增长时，不同频道可以分布到不同服务器上执行。
这样一来，开发者从一开始就按照业务对象划分计算和数据，而不是先编写一个巨大程序，等流量增长之后再考虑如何把它拆分到多台服务器。
Ryan Dahl 在 2026 年 10 月的文章中回忆，他认识到 Durable Objects 的价值时，想到的正是当年 Node.js 的 IRC 聊天服务器。
如果采用一个频道对应一个 Durable Object 的设计，频道天然就成为分布式系统中的一个独立单元。
这个单元有自己的计算逻辑、SQLite 数据库，以及 WebSocket 连接管理能力。
新增频道，相当于增加新的独立对象。系统可以把这些对象分配到更多服务器上。
当然，一个频道内部的处理能力仍然存在上限，但不同频道之间能够相对独立地横向扩展。
Ryan Dahl 看重的正是这一点：分布式扩展不再完全是应用开发完成之后额外添加的基础设施工程，而是从编程模型设计时就被考虑进去。
这解释了为什么 Deno 最终选择兼容 Cloudflare 的接口。
Deno 想解决的问题，并不是如何发明另一套 JavaScript 语法，而是如何让开发者更容易编写和运营分布式应用。
而 Durable Objects 已经为这个问题提供了一套相当成熟的抽象。
但认可 Cloudflare 的编程模型，不意味着只能使用 Cloudflare 的云服务。
一个重要类比是 AWS S3。
S3 最初是 AWS 的对象存储产品，但 S3 API 后来被许多其他存储系统实现。开发者可以使用相似的接口访问不同厂商的对象存储，而不必始终运行在 AWS 上。
Deno 对 Durable Objects 采取了类似思路：沿用已有的开发接口，重新实现背后的执行、调度和持久存储系统。
这就是 celld 的由来。
四、celld：让 Durable Objects 摆脱对单一云平台的依赖
2026 年 8 月 5 日，Ryan Dahl 发布 celld，并以 Apache 2.0 许可证开源。
项目最直接的定位是：
Self-hosted, distributed Durable Objects——可自托管的分布式 Durable Objects。
要理解 celld 的价值，必须区分 Cloudflare 已经开源了什么，以及尚未完整开放什么。
2022 年 9 月，Cloudflare 将 Workers 底层运行时 workerd 开源。
开发者可以在自己的服务器或本地计算机上运行 workerd，执行符合 Workers 编程模型的 JavaScript 程序。
但 workerd 不是完整的 Cloudflare 云平台。
假设一家企业拥有一百台服务器，希望通过这些服务器部署一个使用 Durable Objects 的多人聊天应用。
仅仅安装 workerd，并不会自动形成与 Cloudflare 托管平台相同的分布式系统。
企业还需要解决几个问题：
第一，某个聊天室对象究竟由哪台服务器负责运行？
第二，当用户访问聊天室时，请求如何找到负责这个对象的服务器？
第三，如果服务器突然宕机，其他服务器怎样恢复聊天室的数据并接管请求？
第四，如何避免两台服务器同时认为自己拥有同一个对象的修改权？
这些问题在 Cloudflare 托管版 Durable Objects 中，由 Cloudflare 的基础设施负责。
但当时开源的 workerd 对 Durable Objects 的支持主要局限于单实例场景，并没有直接提供一套适合自托管的、完整的多节点分布式运行系统。
celld 正是为了填补这个缺口。
它不是给 Cloudflare 的服务器安装一个插件，而是提供了另一套独立的运行系统。
开发者可以继续使用 Workers 和 Durable Objects 的编程接口，却把程序部署到自己的虚拟机或服务器集群上。
celld 负责执行代码、确定对象归属、路由请求、保存数据，以及在服务器故障时恢复对象。
它要解决的核心问题，从「怎样运行一个 Durable Object」进一步变成了「怎样让成千上万个 Durable Objects 在多台服务器之间可靠运行」。
五、celld 的技术设计：V8、SQLite、LTX 与对象存储
celld 的架构相当有意思。
传统分布式计算平台通常需要多个基础设施组件，例如分布式数据库、集群协调系统、服务发现、任务调度器和故障检测机制。
这些组件虽然各自成熟，但会增加系统部署和维护的复杂性。
Ryan Dahl 希望把 celld 设计成一个尽可能简单的系统：一个可执行程序，加上一套共享对象存储，就能够组成分布式集群。
它使用 V8 运行 JavaScript，使用 SQLite 保存每个对象的数据，使用 LTX 格式复制数据库变化，再利用兼容 S3 等接口的对象存储完成持久化与集群协调。
其关键设计可以拆成三个部分。
5.1 每个 Cell 都拥有自己的 SQLite
在 celld 中，一个 Cell 可以理解为一个具有独立身份的有状态计算单元，对应 Durable Objects 的基本模型。
每个 Cell 有自己的执行逻辑和 SQLite 数据库。
例如，聊天室 A、B、C 分别拥有各自的 Cell。它们的数据不会全部挤在同一个全局 SQLite 数据库中，而是自然地按照聊天室进行划分。
不同 Cell 可以被分配到不同服务器上运行。
这带来了一种天然的数据分片方式：
不是等数据库变得庞大之后再决定怎样分片，而是应用从一开始就围绕独立业务对象组织数据。
5.2 使用对象存储协调所有权
这是 celld 最独特的技术选择之一。
假设服务器 A 当前负责运行聊天室 001，服务器 B 处于备用状态。
celld 会在共享对象存储中记录聊天室 001 的所有权。
服务器通过对象存储支持的条件写入机制，竞争取得对象的运行权。
例如，服务器 A 成功取得所有权后，服务器 B 就不能同时取得同一个对象的有效所有权。
这依赖对象存储提供足够强的读写一致性和原子条件更新能力，并配合租约、版本纪元等机制隔离旧持有者。
一旦服务器 A 故障，其他服务器可以在满足接管条件后取得所有权。
这种设计避免了 celld 自己再维护一套独立的集群成员管理和分布式共识服务。
需要注意，这并不是说 celld 彻底消除了分布式协调问题，而是把一部分协调工作建立在对象存储已经提供的可靠原语之上。
所以，celld 对底层对象存储的能力有明确要求，并不是任何号称兼容 S3 API 的存储产品都能安全使用。
5.3 使用 LTX 复制 SQLite 数据
解决了对象归属之后，还需要保证服务器故障时不会丢失已经确认的数据。
celld 采用 LTX 记录 SQLite 数据库的持久化变化。
LTX 是一种用于 SQLite 数据库复制的日志格式，与 Ben Johnson 开发的 Litestream 技术体系有关。
Cell 的数据库发生修改后，celld 可以把相应变化复制到其他节点，并持续上传到共享对象存储。
在多节点部署下，celld 可以先让写入在其他节点磁盘上达到规定的持久化条件，再向应用确认成功，之后异步上传到对象存储。
这样能够避免每次数据库写入都必须等待一次对象存储网络往返，也有助于降低对象存储操作成本。
当一个节点故障时，接管节点会根据共享存储和必要的节点日志恢复已经确认的状态，然后重新启动相应 Cell。
celld 的目标之一，是在其明确规定的故障模型和部署条件下，实现已确认写入的零丢失，即 RPO=0。
但这是一项依赖存储可靠性、复制配置和故障假设的技术保证，不能理解为在任何硬件和网络灾难下都绝对不会丢数据。
最终，celld 将这套能力组合成一种简单的部署模型：开发者编写 Workers / Durable Objects 代码，运维人员运行多个 celld 实例，让它们连接共享对象存储，系统负责对象归属、复制和故障转移。
这确实减少了需要单独维护的基础设施组件。
但自托管依然意味着使用者必须负责服务器容量、网络、安全、监控和存储成本，不能把它误认为没有运维工作的 Serverless 托管服务。
而且 celld 仍处于持续完善阶段，虽然已经实现部分 Workers 周边能力，却不能直接视为完整 Cloudflare 云平台的替代品。
六、从竞争到汇合：Deno 为什么最终加入 Cloudflare？
至此，Deno 和 Cloudflare 的技术路线开始出现一种微妙的关系。
Cloudflare 拥有已经被大量应用使用的 Workers 编程模型、成熟的托管平台，以及开源的 workerd 运行时。
Deno 团队则通过 celld，探索了如何在 Cloudflare 之外，用较少的基础设施组件实现分布式 Durable Objects。
一方拥有成熟的编程模型和云平台，另一方提出了自托管分布式运行的新实现。
双方并没有在完全相同的方向上重复建设，而是在同一个技术模型的不同部分形成了互补。
2026 年 10 月 9 日，Ryan Dahl 和 Cloudflare Workers 核心设计者 Kenton Varda 联合宣布，Deno 团队加入 Cloudflare，并计划整合 celld 与 workerd。
这里的重点不是使用 Deno Runtime 替换 workerd。
两者原本都是独立的 JavaScript 运行时，Cloudflare 没有必要为了获得 celld 的分布式能力，就放弃自己的运行时。
整合的目标，是让 workerd 已有的代码执行能力，与 celld 探索的跨服务器对象调度、状态复制和故障恢复机制结合起来。
这使同一种 Workers / Durable Objects 编程模型，有机会同时服务于 Cloudflare 自己的托管网络和客户自己的基础设施。
但这也意味着 Deno 团队必须重新分配研发资源。
Ryan Dahl 在公告中宣布，Deno Runtime 将继续获得一年的月度维护更新，随后停止由原团队继续开发；Deno Deploy 将在六个月后停止运营，并协助付费客户迁移到 Cloudflare Workers。
Deno 运行时仍会保持开源，JSR 包注册平台则计划继续运营，相关基础设施迁移至 Cloudflare。
这是一项相当重大的取舍。
毕竟，Deno 最初就是为了挑战 Node.js 而诞生，Deno Deploy 也是团队多年建设的商业产品。
如今，团队却选择将未来的主要研发力量投入另一家公司的编程模型和运行平台。
从 Ryan Dahl 自己对这段历史的回顾来看，这并不是突然放弃初心，而是他认为终于找到了比改进单个运行时更重要的问题。
Node.js 曾经降低了异步网络编程的复杂性。
Deno 希望降低 JavaScript 开发和运行环境的复杂性。
Deno Deploy 试图进一步降低应用部署的复杂性。
而 celld 想要解决的，是怎样让应用在多台服务器之间分布计算、协调状态，同时不要求每个开发团队自行搭建复杂的分布式基础设施。
沿着这条路线看，Durable Objects 的吸引力恰恰在于：它不是又增加了一个需要开发者学习的基础设施组件，而是
将一组原本复杂的分布式能力，浓缩成相对简单的编程抽象。
七、Cloudflare 为什么愿意让自己的技术走向开放？
从竞争关系看，celld 原本也可以成为 Cloudflare 的威胁。
如果开发者能够在自己的服务器上运行兼容 Workers 和 Durable Objects 的程序，就可能不再需要购买 Cloudflare 的计算服务。
但 Cloudflare 对此给出了另一种商业解释。
Kenton Varda 在双方联合公告中表示，Cloudflare 并不认为让 Workers 应用难以迁移是一个值得追求的优势。
相反，对于某些大型企业，不能迁移恰恰是拒绝采用一项技术的重要原因。
他提到，2022 年 Cloudflare 向 Shopify 等客户推广 Workers for Platforms 时，对方明确要求底层运行时必须开源，否则不愿在其上构建核心业务。
Cloudflare 随后开放了 workerd。
按照 Kenton Varda 的说法，确实已经有客户利用 workerd 离开 Cloudflare，但这种可迁移能力也让更多企业愿意在一开始采用 Workers。
celld 将这条路线进一步推进。
它使 Durable Objects 不只是 Cloudflare 托管平台提供的一种服务，也成为能够在其他基础设施上实现的编程模型。
不过，这与真正形成跨厂商通用标准仍有距离。
celld 当前的 API 兼容范围、运行时行为、可用性保证和运维成熟度，都还需要继续完善。企业也不能假设一个深度使用 Cloudflare 各类云服务的应用，今天就能够不做任何修改地迁移到 celld。
因此，双方真正宣布的是技术整合方向，而不是已经完成了一套全面兼容的开放平台。
这次整合最值得关注的地方，在于 Cloudflare 和 Deno 对未来服务器应用的判断开始趋于一致。
应用开发者需要的，或许不只是越来越快的 JavaScript 运行时，也不只是越来越便宜的计算资源，而是一套让分布式计算和状态管理变得更容易使用的编程模型。
Deno 从最初的 Node.js 挑战者，逐渐成为这种模型的推动者。
Cloudflare 则希望在继续提供托管计算服务的同时，让 Workers 和 Durable Objects 被更多基础设施所支持。
从这一意义上说，celld 并不是 Durable Objects 的下一代替代品，也不是 Deno 在 Cloudflare 产品之上增加的普通配套工具。
它代表了一种重要尝试：
把原本由单一云厂商提供的有状态 Serverless 能力，转化为能够由不同基础设施承载的软件运行模型。
（后记：至于为什么 Cloudflare 愿意投入资源，让开发者更容易脱离自己的托管平台；为什么又在 2026 年接连整合 Astro、VoidZero/Vite 和 Deno 三支团队，则已经超出了运行时技术本身。这背后涉及的是 Cloudflare 对未来应用开发工具链、开发者入口，以及 AI 时代云计算市场的一次更大范围的布局。）

en.subtitle: Cloudflare signals a determined push into the JavaScript toolchain

text.text:
Cloudflare has acquired Deno to improve the Workers programming model.

What is Deno? Node.js creator Ryan Dahl’s next-generation JavaScript/TypeScript runtime: secure by default, native TypeScript support, integrated tools, and npm compatibility. Deno Deploy provides edge hosting. In August this year the team also released celld, an open-source, self-hosted implementation of the Workers and Durable Objects model.

Was the acquisition wise? I think so: it fills a specific gap. Cloudflare acknowledged that open-sourcing workerd had not established a strong self-hosting ecosystem, especially for Durable Objects. celld is the path Deno explored. The acquisition brings deep V8-runtime expertise and addresses lock-in concerns, potentially making enterprise adoption easier.
What Is Cloudflare Workers?
Workers is a flagship Cloudflare product: a whole set of cloud computing services.
It provides serverless execution of JavaScript and other supported code.
It can be divided into four parts:

cells.text: Executes JavaScript and supplies isolated environments
Runs code around the world, closer to users
Receives requests, allocates resources, scales execution, and manages deployment
D1 databases, R2 object storage, Durable Objects, and other application services

text.text: Workers is the core compute product, workerd its underlying runtime, Durable Objects a specialized compute capability, and D1, R2, and KV part of its surrounding service ecosystem.
What Is Serverless?
Developers write code while the provider manages servers and scaling, supplying resources according to usage. Servers still exist; their management is hidden from developers.
How Does It Differ from Traditional Servers?
Suppose a website has 100,000 daily visitors with uneven traffic.
A traditional cloud server, such as AWS EC2:
You rent a server and deploy the backend.
It runs even with no visitors.
A sudden 10,000 visitors may overwhelm it.
You configure scaling, load balancing, and related mechanisms.
Billing is generally based on server running time.
Serverless, such as AWS Lambda:
You submit request-handling code.
No requests may mean no corresponding function compute use.
A request triggers execution.
The platform attempts to scale for 10,000 simultaneous requests, subject to concurrency limits.
Charges generally reflect invocations, duration, memory, and similar factors.
What Is Conventional Serverless?
In a narrow sense, conventional serverless means FaaS, exemplified by AWS Lambda’s 2014 launch.
Three typical characteristics are:
Event-driven execution: HTTP requests, uploads, or schedules trigger code.
Statelessness: the next execution cannot rely on previously retained memory.
Short invocation lifecycle: a call finishes, and its environment may be reused or destroyed.
This explains the emphasis on functions rather than continuously running servers.
Which Applications Suit Serverless?

The best fits share relatively independent tasks, unpredictable traffic, and no need to occupy a server continuously. Conversely, constant intensive compute, complex long-lived memory state, or numerous persistent connections may suit traditional FaaS poorly. Sustained high load is not necessarily cheaper there.
What Is workerd?
It uses lightweight V8 isolates for serverless execution at global edge locations, emphasizing low latency and fast startup.
It resembles lightweight virtualization in some respects.
Its isolation layer differs from VMware or Docker.

cells.text: A virtual machine capable of running a full OS

text.text: The shared idea is:
Programs share underlying resources while retaining isolation instead of each requiring a fully separate environment.
workerd is a multitenant JavaScript runtime built on isolates, not general-purpose virtualization software.
Cloudflare did not invent isolates; they are provided by Google’s V8 engine.
Cloudflare combines them with security restrictions, request processing, and resource management to host many customers on shared servers.
V8 Isolate
Imagine one server running JavaScript written by Zhang San and Li Si.
Containers give each a relatively independent OS-level environment.
Two isolates in one workerd process provide separate JavaScript memory without starting a full process for each, generally reducing overhead and startup time.
An isolate alone is not a full security sandbox. It primarily separates JavaScript state; workerd also restricts operating-system access.
Containers isolate at OS level, isolates inside the engine, while sandboxing describes the intended security effect.
Using lightweight isolation extensively is one characteristic of Workers.
workerd Versus Other Runtimes
Its defining focus is dense, secure multitenant execution.
Compared with Node.js, Deno, and Bun:
Node.js, Deno, and Bun primarily execute general-purpose JavaScript programs.
workerd primarily lets cloud platforms share resources safely and efficiently among many customers’ programs.
It targets three goals:
Density: many isolates in one process reduce overhead.
Isolation: customer programs are separated and tightly permissioned.
Fast startup: environments are created on demand as cloud request loads change.
Other runtimes can support multitenancy too, with additional isolation and management.
Its goal is not a better general Node.js, but a runtime suited to large-scale hosting of customer code.
workerd is open source and not cloud-only.
On Cloudflare servers, it powers Workers hosting.
On your computer, it supports local development and testing.
What Are Durable Objects?
They introduce uniquely identified compute objects with consistent state and persistent storage into Workers.

They complement Workers’ stateful coordination rather than replace Workers. Serverless exploration continues beyond hiding servers, asking whether persistent, complex applications can also become convenient without server management.
Cloudflare designed them to address serverless state management.
They provide stateful programming capable of coordinating concurrent requests.
They are specialized Workers with identity, storage, and evolving state.
Traditional development could already solve these problems. The change is how developers organize and implement the capabilities.
Think of an object as a small backend program with identity, stored data, and the ability to receive requests.

Conventional serverless centers on invocations; Durable Objects center on ongoing business objects. That matters for chat, collaboration, games, live services, and agents with independent memory and task state.
Example: A Multiplayer Online Whiteboard
Several people open the same board and draw or write. A line drawn by one person appears almost immediately for others.
What problems arise?
When Ming draws a line, the server must distribute the change.
When Hong draws simultaneously, it must coordinate their actions.
Membership changes require tracking who is online.
Persistent board contents must be recoverable after refresh.
All these operations concern one shared board.
How Would Conventional Development Handle This?
You combine several components:
Backend logic handles user actions.
WebSockets deliver real-time changes.
A database saves the board.
Other coordination mechanisms synchronize concurrent actions correctly.
This is viable and commonplace.
These are ordinary backend requirements; you can use a traditional backend and database without Durable Objects.
What Do Durable Objects Do Here?
Assign one object to each board.
It supplies connection management, operation coordination, and persistence without requiring you to construct a dedicated coordination backend for each board.

With ordinary Workers, messages from users A and B may reach instances on different machines. They do not share reliable memory: membership, recent messages, and notifications require databases, Redis, messaging, or similar systems. With Durable Objects, each chat room can instead have its own object.
The room has a stable logical owner.
Requests from any of its users can locate that same room object to coordinate messages and state.
Furthermore:
A thousand rooms can have a thousand independent objects.
Each has its own persistent storage.
No dedicated server is required per room.
Objects can sleep without requests and restart on access while retaining persisted data.
The core value is colocating business compute and state management under automatic platform scheduling.
How Workers, workerd, and Durable Objects Relate
Workers is the product, workerd the runtime, and Durable Objects stateful compute built on that runtime.
An analogy:
Workers: the hosted program-execution service you rent.
workerd: the runtime executing JavaScript/Wasm.
Durable Objects: capabilities that add management of a specific object’s state to cloud execution.
Ordinary requests may run in different instances without shared reliable memory. A Durable Object ID identifies one logical instance whose state consistency is managed by the platform.
It is not simply a database or arbitrary SQLite attached to a Worker. It combines compute, state, identity, and concurrency coordination.
If 100 customers compete for the final ticket, one object coordinating inventory makes avoiding overselling easier. Distributed ordinary handlers require additional coordination.
When Would You Use It?
Does the application have something many users must operate on concurrently, sharing state and coordinating in real time?
For example:
An online whiteboard: one board.
A multiplayer game: one room.
Live chat: one chat room.
Collaborative editing: one shared document.
Each can have its own object.
An ordinary blog, profile display, product list, or form saved to a database usually does not need this.

Durable Objects assign a backend instance responsibility for one application object’s live state and coordination. They simplify implementation rather than enable something traditional development could not do.
What Is Cloudflare Trying to Achieve with These Acquisitions?
It is filling Workers’ gaps in three different areas.
Some are technical capabilities; others are developer entry points.
Workers already ran JavaScript efficiently and inexpensively in the cloud.
Becoming a complete development platform required addressing three concerns.

cells.text: Easier creation of websites deployable to Workers
JavaScript development, debugging, testing, and builds
Aligns local and hosted environments, eases deployment, and makes Workers a natural default earlier in the workflow
JavaScript runtimes, cloud hosting, and later celld
Makes Workers easier to run on private servers as well as Cloudflare
A longer-term openness strategy: expand a proprietary model’s user base toward an industry standard, then capture hosting demand

text.text: Why Acquire VoidZero/Vite?
Primarily to participate in a major JavaScript tooling entry point, rather than fix runtime defects, and thereby grow Workers adoption and revenue.
It wants Workers to be a more natural deployment choice, an explicit direction in the acquisition announcement.
Vite remains open source and supports other clouds. Cloudflare competes for developer choice, not exclusive use of Vite.
A Vite site can be deployed to AWS, Vercel, or Cloudflare.
Cloudflare seeks to use Vite’s leading position and a smooth workerd-based local experience to make Workers deployment natural from the Vite stage onward.
The deal offers three advantages:
The core development team: direct participation in Vite and its broader toolchain.
Lower deployment friction: build development, build, and deployment tooling on Vite.
AI-coding adoption: agents also create and test applications with Vite, and Cloudflare wants to host them.
How Vite and workerd Cooperate
This is not Vite fixing a defective runtime.
Consider developing a website:
Vite starts the local development environment and updates the browser as code changes.
workerd executes backend JavaScript locally using the same mechanisms as Workers.
Cloudflare’s Vite plugin connects them.
After deployment, workerd also executes the hosted application.
The local environment does not merely pretend to be the cloud: both actually use workerd.
That reduces cases where code works locally but fails after deployment.
Why Acquire Deno?
The motivation differs from the Vite deal.
VoidZero mainly provides the Vite product and developer reach.
Deno brings celld, rather than its general runtime, to strengthen execution outside Cloudflare infrastructure.
What Is celld?
A distributed system from Deno that deploys Workers and Durable Objects on private servers.

celld is open source and brings the Workers/Durable Objects model to developers’ own infrastructure. V8 executes code, each Cell gets SQLite, and replicated logs plus object storage provide persistence and recovery. A Cell conceptually corresponds to a Durable Object. Developers can use their own VMs, clusters, and buckets for comparable stateful serverless applications instead of depending entirely on Cloudflare hosting.
Which Durable Objects Problem Does celld Address?
A common misconception is:
celld did not discover a state-management defect and invent a superior replacement.
It first addresses the model’s dependence on Cloudflare infrastructure.
Running 10,000 objects on private servers and storage otherwise requires implementing the distributed management Cloudflare normally supplies.
For example:
Which server runs which object?
Who takes over after a crash?
Where is the latest SQLite state recovered from?
How are simultaneous owners prevented?
Cloudflare already handles these. celld recreates the guarantees on developers’ infrastructure.
How Does celld Do This?

Conventional serverless uses invocations as compute units. Durable Objects promote identified stateful objects; celld demonstrates that this model can be implemented on private clusters using V8, SQLite, LTX, and object storage.
What Gap Did Cloudflare Have?
workerd executes JavaScript and supports multiple isolates.
Workers is the broader cloud platform built on it.
Installing open-source workerd on 100 servers is not enough to recreate a comparable service.
Placement, inter-server coordination, persistence, and recovery still require complex distributed systems engineering.
What Did the Deno Team Bring?
The key is its new celld project, not Deno Runtime.
It aims to let complete Workers/Durable Objects applications run on private servers without depending on Cloudflare’s cloud.
Enterprises could reproduce the development experience on their own infrastructure.

cells.text: Manage Durable Objects across multiple machines

text.text: The final row matters: Cloudflare is expanding self-hosting, not open-sourcing its entire cloud.
workerd already answers how one machine efficiently runs many JavaScript programs. The Deno team helps answer how many machines run them together.
Cloudflare wants comparable private-deployment freedom for Workers.
The difficulty is that Workers includes scheduling, communication, and persistence across machines, not just JavaScript execution.
Open-source workerd primarily addressed execution.
celld addresses multinode coordination, particularly stateful objects distributed across servers.
Cloudflare explicitly acknowledged that the open-source Durable Objects implementation was mainly single-instance and did not directly provide hosted distributed scaling.
The goal is a privately deployable distributed Workers platform, not an open copy of every Cloudflare service.
What Happens to Deno Runtime?
Deno competed with Node.js, while Cloudflare already had workerd.
It does not plan to replace workerd with Deno.
Deno announced:
One further year of runtime maintenance, then an end to official development.
Six further months of Deno Deploy operation, then closure.
The team shifts to Workers and Durable Objects development.
What Is the Strategic Objective?
My assessment is that Cloudflare wants Workers to evolve from its own hosted product into an application platform others can deploy too.
This complements Vite in two directions:
Vite encourages more developers to choose Workers.
Deno helps Workers run independently of Cloudflare infrastructure.
Why Enable Private Deployment When Hosting Generates Revenue?
Cloudflare believes the freedom to leave can encourage more customers to join.
An enterprise considering Workers for core operations may worry about price increases, service problems, and inability to migrate.
Cloudflare wants to offer two options:
Paid hosting: managed servers, the global network, automatic scaling, and related services.
Self-hosting: infrastructure control, but responsibility for servers, operations, and scaling.
The bet is that reduced lock-in concerns encourage adoption, with most customers still choosing convenient paid hosting.

This is grounded in the announcement: Shopify and other large customers demanded an open runtime in 2022 before adoption. Cloudflare opened workerd and acknowledged some customers used it to leave, while still considering the overall trade worthwhile.
The broader strategy reduces adoption risk and promotes Workers from a proprietary cloud product toward a general execution model.
It aims to earn revenue from hosting and operating that model, not merely retaining users through closure.
workerd has been open source since 2022 and can be self-hosted, but it is not the complete Workers cloud platform.
Why Do Customers Choose Workers?
Three main benefits:
Efficiency: dense JavaScript execution uses fewer resources than separate-process deployments.
Convenience: hosted customers need not manage servers or scaling.
Distributed development: Durable Objects simplify real-time communication and state.
These are advantages emphasized by Cloudflare.
Why Self-Host?
An enterprise may prefer Workers programming while using its own servers instead of renting Cloudflare compute.
Open-source workerd has enabled that since 2022.
But complete distributed management was missing.
A 100-server chat service must decide room placement, route requests, and recover data and execution after failure. Hosted Workers supplies these capabilities.
Self-hosted workerd’s single-instance objects did not directly provide multinode scaling, leaving those concerns to operators.
A Prediction of Cloudflare’s AI-Era Strategy
It is competing for software production and execution infrastructure, beyond conventional cloud demand.
Lower AI development costs may create many more applications and agents. Cloudflare wants both human- and AI-written software to adopt its toolchain and execution model.
Cloudflare vs Vercel
Astro competes for frameworks used in AI web creation, broadening its ecosystem and directly challenging Next.js/Vercel.
VoidZero/Vite competes for development, testing, and build tools, reaching beyond a single framework.
Deno/celld promotes a self-hostable Workers standard and differentiation from Vercel hosting.
Vite is particularly important:
Widespread coding-agent use gives Cloudflare influence over deployment destinations.
It need not build a framework superior to Next.js in every respect. Vite reaches competing framework ecosystems, whose applications can then be attracted to Workers.
Vercel expands from Next.js, frontend frameworks, and deployment toward AI coding, agents, and compute infrastructure.
Cloudflare expands from networking and compute toward frameworks, tools, and AI-coding ecosystems.
For human developers, agents, and competitors alike, its commercial goal remains more Workers applications, some converting to paid cloud customers.
Summary
Cloudflare seeks to become a major participant in AI-era development toolchains and execution standards, not simply a provider of compute resources.

云端运行 JavaScript 等代码的 Serverless 计算服务
可以分成四个部分：

cells.text: 真正执行 JavaScript 代码，提供隔离环境
在世界各地运行这些代码，让用户就近访问
接收请求、分配计算资源、自动扩容、管理程序部署
数据库 D1、对象存储 R2、Durable Objects 等，供程序使用

text.text: 总结：Workers 是 Cloudflare 的核心计算产品，workerd 是它的底层运行时，Durable Objects 是它的一种特殊计算能力，而 D1、R2、KV 等则构成周边云服务生态。
Serversless 是什么？
Serverless 的本质是：开发者只管写代码，不管服务器怎么运行、扩容、缩容；云厂商按实际使用量提供计算资源。注意，Serverless 不是没有服务器，而是服务器的管理对开发者隐藏了。
传统服务器和 Serverless 有什么区别？
假设你开发一个网站，每天有 10 万人访问，但是访问量很不均匀。
传统云服务器（例如 AWS EC2）：
你租一台服务器，把后端程序部署上去。
没人访问，服务器也在运行。
突然来 1 万人，服务器可能撑不住。
你需要配置扩容、负载均衡等机制。
通常按服务器使用时间付费。
Serverless（例如 AWS Lambda）：
你只提交处理请求的代码。
没人访问，可以不消耗对应的函数计算资源。
来一个请求，云平台就执行你的代码。
同时来 1 万个请求，云平台尝试自动扩容处理（受并发限制）。
通常按调用次数、执行时间、内存等计费。
传统 Serverless 是什么？
狭义的传统 Serverless，通常指以 2014 年推出的 AWS Lambda 为代表的 FaaS（Function as a Service，函数即服务）。
它有三个典型特点：
事件驱动：来了 HTTP 请求、文件上传或定时事件，才触发代码执行。
无状态：不能指望下一次执行还能使用上一次留在内存里的数据。
短生命周期：每次调用执行完就结束，运行环境可能被复用，但也可能随时被销毁。
这就是为什么传统 Serverless 特别强调函数，而不是一台长期运行的服务器。
什么应用适合 Serverless？

它最适合的应用具有一个共同点：
计算任务相对独立，访问量不稳定，不需要长期占据一台服务器。
反过来，如果一个程序需要 7×24 小时持续高强度计算、长期维持复杂内存状态，或者有大量持续连接，那么传统 FaaS 往往不理想。持续高负载下也未必比服务器便宜。
workerd 是什么？
使用轻量级 V8 Isolate，在全球边缘节点运行 Serverless 代码，强调低延迟与快速启动。
Cloudflare 的 workerd 确实很像一种轻量级虚拟化技术。
但它与 VMware、Docker 的隔离层级不同。

cells.text: 一台虚拟计算机，能运行完整操作系统
一个相对独立的应用运行环境
一块独立的 JavaScript 执行空间

text.text: 它们的共同思路是：
让多个原本需要独立运行环境的程序，共享底层资源，同时保持隔离。
workerd 不是通用虚拟化软件，而是基于 V8 Isolate 构建的多租户 JavaScript 运行时。
V8 Isolate 并不是 Cloudflare 发明的。它本来就是 Google V8 引擎提供的机制。
Cloudflare 的工作，是利用这个机制，配合安全限制、请求处理和资源管理，构建一个能让大量客户共享服务器资源的云计算平台。
V8 Isolate
假设 Cloudflare 有一台服务器，需要同时运行张三和李四写的 JavaScript 程序。
使用容器：可以给两人分别创建一个容器。每个容器拥有相对独立的操作系统运行环境。
使用 V8 Isolate：可以在同一个 workerd 进程内部创建两个 Isolate，让两段 JavaScript 拥有彼此独立的内存空间，而无需分别启动完整的进程。这样通常更轻量，启动也更快。
重要区别：V8 Isolate 本身不等于完整的安全沙箱。它主要隔离 JavaScript 的执行状态。Cloudflare 还需要通过 workerd 限制程序访问操作系统的能力。
可以这样理解：容器是在操作系统层面做隔离，Isolate 是在 JavaScript 引擎内部做隔离，而沙箱描述的是希望实现的安全效果。
Cloudflare Workers 的技术特色之一，就是大量使用这种更轻量的隔离方式来运行客户代码。
workerd VS 其他运行时
workerd 最突出的特点，就是专门为「高密度、安全的多租户运行」设计。
相比 Node.js、Deno、Bun：
Node.js / Deno / Bun：主要面向通用 JavaScript 程序的执行。
workerd：主要面向云平台，让大量不同客户的 JavaScript 程序安全、高效地共享服务器资源。
它的设计围绕三个目标：
高密度：一个进程容纳大量 V8 Isolate，降低资源开销。
强隔离：不同客户的程序互不干扰，并受到严格的权限限制。
快速启动：按需创建运行环境，适应云端请求负载的变化。
当然，其他运行时也能用于多租户系统，只是需要额外的隔离和管理机制。
所以，workerd 的核心定位不是做一个更好的通用 Node.js，而是做一个更适合云厂商大规模托管客户代码的 JavaScript 运行时。
注意：workerd 本身是开源的，并不是只能在云端运行。
在 Cloudflare 的服务器上运行：支撑 Cloudflare Workers 云服务。
在你自己的电脑上运行：让你在本地开发、测试 Workers 程序。
Durable Objects 是什么？
在 Workers 生态中引入具有唯一身份、状态一致性、持久存储的计算对象。

Durable Objects 不是取代 Workers，而是补充 Workers 所欠缺的有状态协调能力。
所以，Serverless 的技术探索并没有止步于「把服务器隐藏起来」，而是继续探索：
能不能既不让开发者管理服务器，又能方便地运行具有持续状态的复杂应用？
Durable Objects 正是在尝试回答这个问题。
Durable Objects 是 Cloudflare 为解决 Serverless 的「状态管理」问题而设计的一种计算模型。
Durable Objects 是 Cloudflare Workers 体系里的一种“有状态、能协调并发请求”的编程机制。
是一种特殊的 Worker，拥有独立身份、持久存储，能管理持续变化的状态
Durable Objects 并不是解决了一个传统开发完全解决不了的问题。传统技术早就能解决这些问题；它改变的是开发者组织和实现这些功能的方式。
Durable Object 可以理解为一个有独立身份、能保存数据、并且能接收请求的“小型后端程序”。

传统 Serverless 围绕「一次函数调用」组织计算，而 Durable Objects 围绕「一个具有持续身份和状态的业务对象」组织计算。
这对聊天室、多人协作、游戏、实时服务，乃至需要独立记忆和任务状态的 AI Agent，都很有意义。
场景举例：开发一个多人在线白板
想象你开发了一个网站，允许几个人同时打开同一块白板，在上面画画、写字。一个人画了一条线，其他人几乎立刻就能看到。
这个功能会遇到什么问题？
小明画了一条线，服务器需要把这条线的变化告诉其他人。
小红同时也在画画，服务器需要协调两个人的操作。
有人加入或离开白板，系统需要知道当前有哪些人在线。
如果白板内容需要保存，刷新页面后还得能恢复。
注意：这些事情都围绕着同一块白板发生。
普通开发通常怎么做？
你需要自己组合一些东西：
后端程序：处理用户发来的操作。
WebSocket：让服务器可以实时向用户推送变化。
数据库：保存白板内容。
其他协调机制：让不同用户的操作能够正确同步。
这套方案完全可行，而且是常见的开发方式。
它不是一种特殊业务，你完全可以不用它，采用传统的后端程序加数据库。
Durable Objects 在这里做什么？
你可以给每块白板安排一个 Durable Object。
你不必自己搭建一整套专门负责这块白板的后端协调系统。Durable Objects 提供了这种机制：它可以管理连接、协调操作，并使用持久化存储保存数据。

使用普通 Workers：
用户 A 发消息，Worker 处理请求；用户 B 发消息，可能由另一台机器上的 Worker 处理。
问题是：这些 Worker 不共享一份可靠的内存状态。谁在聊天室里？最新消息是什么？如何实时通知其他人？
传统解决办法是引入数据库、Redis、消息系统等。
使用 Durable Objects：
你可以为每个聊天室创建一个独立的 Durable Object。
重点：这个聊天室有了一个固定的逻辑归属。
无论三个用户的请求从哪里进来，都能找到同一个聊天室对象，由它协调消息和状态。
而且：
1000 个聊天室，可以拥有 1000 个独立的 Durable Object 实例。
每个对象都有自己的持久存储。
不需要给每个聊天室准备一台服务器。
没有请求时，对象可以休眠；下次访问再启动，持久化的数据还在。
这就是它的核心价值：把某项业务的计算逻辑和状态管理放在一起，交给平台自动调度。
Workers、workerd、Durable Objects 的关系
这里最容易混淆的是：Workers 是产品，workerd 是运行时，Durable Objects 是建立在 Workers 运行时之上的有状态计算能力。
可以类比：
Workers：你租用的云端程序执行服务。
workerd：负责执行 JavaScript/Wasm 的引擎。
Durable Objects：让云端程序不仅能执行计算，还能管理一个特定对象的状态。
但有一个关键区别：普通 Workers 的请求可能在不同实例上执行，不能指望各次请求共享可靠的内存；而同一个 Durable Object ID 对应一个逻辑实例，并由平台保证它的状态一致性。
所以，DO 不是普通数据库，也不是给 Worker 随便加个 SQLite。它是「计算 + 状态 + 唯一身份 + 并发协调」的组合。
例如，100 人同时抢最后一张票，让对应的 DO 统一处理库存扣减，就更容易避免超卖；仅靠普通 Workers 分散处理，就必须额外解决并发协调问题。
所以，究竟什么时候会用它？
应用里，是否有一个东西，需要很多用户同时操作，而且这些操作必须共享状态、实时协调？
例如：
多人在线白板：一块白板。
多人游戏：一个游戏房间。
实时聊天：一个聊天室。
协同编辑：一份正在被多人编辑的文档。
这些东西都可以各自拥有一个 Durable Object。
反过来，如果你只是开发一个博客，展示文章、用户资料、商品列表，用户提交表单后保存到数据库，通常就不需要 Durable Objects。
一句话总结：Durable Objects 是 Cloudflare 提供的一种机制，让你能给应用中的某个特定对象安排一个负责其实时状态与操作协调的后端实例。 它的价值在于简化这类功能的实现，而不是让传统开发做不到的事情突然变得可行。
Cloudflare 这一系列大动作是要干什么？
Cloudflare 在补 Workers 的短板。但三笔收购补的是三个完全不同的地方。
有些收购是在补 Workers 的技术能力，有些是在争夺开发者入口。
Workers 原本擅长的是：在云端高效、低成本地运行 JavaScript 程序。
但 Cloudflare 想把它发展成一个完整的软件开发平台，就有三个问题需要解决。

cells.text: 对 Workers 有什么帮助
让开发者更方便地创建能部署到 Workers 的网站
JavaScript 开发、调试、测试、构建工具
让本地开发环境和 Workers 云端运行环境更一致，降低部署难度。在 Vite 阶段就引导用户默认部署到 Workers。
JS 运行时、云部署，后来开发 celld
让 Workers 不只在 Cloudflare 云上运行，也更容易在企业自己的服务器上运行。
欲扬先抑，欲擒故纵。变独门技术为行业标准，扩大用户基数，放长线钓大鱼。

text.text: 收购 VoidZero（Vite）意在何为？
主要不是为了弥补 workerd 的技术缺陷，而是为了掌握 JavaScript 开发工具链的重要入口。进而给 Cloudflare Workers 带来更多用户和收入。
Cloudflare 希望开发者在完成开发后，能够更自然地选择 Workers 部署应用。这也是 Cloudflare 官方收购公告明确提出的方向。
另外，Vite 仍然开源，仍可部署到其他云平台。Cloudflare 争取的是开发者的选择，不是获得 Vite 的排他使用权。
假设你用 Vite 开发了一个网站。开发完成后，可以选择部署到 AWS、Vercel 或 Cloudflare。
Cloudflare 想改变的是：Vite 作为前端工程化领域的绝对霸主。Cloudflare 通过把 workerd 的本地开发体验做的流程无比，让开发者在 Vite 阶段就被引导直接部署到 Workers 上。
收购 VoidZero（Vite）有三个价值：
获得核心研发团队：直接参与 Vite 及其整套工具链的发展。
降低部署门槛：把 Cloudflare 的开发、构建、部署工具直接建立在 Vite 之上。
争取 AI Coding 用户：AI Agent 也大量使用 Vite 创建、测试应用。Cloudflare 希望这些应用最终运行在自己的云平台上。
Vite 和 workerd 如何配合
不是 workerd 有技术缺陷，需要 Vite 来补。
假设你正在开发一个网站：
Vite 帮你启动本地开发环境，让你在浏览器里看到网页，修改代码就能看到变化。
workerd 在你的电脑上执行网站的后端 JavaScript，采用和 Cloudflare Workers 相同的运行机制。
Cloudflare 的「Vite 插件」把两者连接起来，让它们协同工作。
这样，开发完成后，你把程序部署到 Cloudflare，线上依然由 workerd 执行。
所以，不是 workerd 在本地「假装」成云端，而是云端和本地都真正使用 workerd。
这也正是 Cloudflare 整合 Vite 的价值之一：减少「本地能运行，部署到云端却出问题」的情况。
收购 deno 意在何为
收购 Deno 团队，和收购 Vite 的目的完全不同。
收购 VoidZero 公司：主要看中了 Vite 产品，用来争夺开发者入口。
收购 Deno 公司：要的是产品 celld，而不是 Deno 运行时。主要是增强 Workers 的底层能力，让 Workers 能更容易地运行在 Cloudflare 以外的服务器上。
Celld 是什么
Deno 团队开发的分布式运行系统，让 Workers、Durable Objects 等可以部署在自己的服务器上

celld 是 Deno 团队开发的开源项目。
它想做的事情是：
把 Cloudflare 的 Workers + Durable Objects 这套编程模型，搬到开发者自己的服务器上。
celld 使用 V8 执行代码，为每个 Cell 提供 SQLite，通过复制日志和对象存储来管理持久化与故障恢复。一个 Cell 在概念上对应一个 Durable Object。
这样开发者就可以用自己的虚拟机、集群和存储桶，部署类似 Cloudflare 的有状态 Serverless 应用，而不必完全依赖 Cloudflare 托管环境。
celld 又解决了 Durable Objects 什么问题？
这里有一个容易产生的误解：
celld 并不是发现了 Durable Objects 的状态管理缺陷，然后发明了更好的状态机制。
它首先解决的是：Durable Objects 这套编程模型主要依赖 Cloudflare 自己的基础设施运行。
如果你希望用自己的服务器、自己的存储，运行一万个这样的对象，就需要自行实现 Cloudflare 原本在背后承担的分布式管理工作。
例如：
哪台服务器负责运行哪个 DO？
一台服务器突然宕机，其他服务器怎么接管？
接管后，SQLite 的最新数据从哪里恢复？
如何防止两台服务器同时修改同一个对象？
这些事情 Cloudflare 本身就会处理。celld 的价值是：在开发者自己的基础设施上重新实现这些保证。
celld 怎么解决的？
传统 Serverless 的计算单位是「函数调用」，Durable Objects 将计算单位提升为「有身份、有状态的对象」，而 celld 则进一步证明，这种模型可以用 V8 + SQLite + LTX + 对象存储，在自己的服务器集群中实现。
Cloudflare 原来有什么问题？
workerd：负责运行 JavaScript，支持多个 Isolate。
Workers：Cloudflare 在 workerd 之上建立的整套云计算平台。
虽然 workerd 已经开源，但假设你有 100 台自己的服务器，想搭建类似 Cloudflare Workers 的服务：光安装 workerd 远远不够。
你还需要解决：程序放在哪台服务器运行？服务器之间怎么协调？程序的数据怎么保存？机器故障后怎么恢复？这些都是复杂的分布式系统问题。
Deno 团队带来了什么？
关键不是 Deno Runtime，而是他们开发的一个新项目：celld。
celld 补的是：为了让开发者不依赖 Cloudflare 的云服务器，也能在自己的服务器上运行完整的 Workers + Durable Objects 应用。
让企业能在自己的服务器上复现整套 Workers 开发体验，而不必完全依赖 Cloudflare 云。

cells.text: 跨多台服务器管理 Durable Objects
接近完整的 Cloudflare 云平台

text.text: 最后一行很重要：Cloudflare 并不是准备把自己的整个云平台开源，而是把 Workers 的自托管能力做得更完整。
所以，这笔交易的技术目的可以简单概括为：workerd 开源，已经解决了「一台机器怎样高效运行大量 JavaScript 程序」，Deno 团队要帮助它进一步解决「很多台机器怎样协同运行这些程序」。
Cloudflare 希望 Workers 也具有类似的本地部署自由度。
但难点在于：Workers 不只是执行 JavaScript，还涉及程序在多台服务器之间的调度、通信、状态保存等。
以前开源的 workerd 主要解决代码执行问题。
Deno 团队带来的 celld，则试图解决多台服务器之间的协调问题。特别是让 Durable Objects 能跨服务器运行、保存状态。
Cloudflare 官方也明确承认：目前开源 workerd 的 Durable Objects 实现主要局限于单实例，无法直接实现其云平台上的分布式扩展能力。
因此，这次收购的目标不是开放整套 Cloudflare 云服务，而是：让企业可以在自己的服务器上，搭建一个支持 Workers 编程模型的分布式运行平台。
那 Deno Runtime 怎么处理？
Deno 原本是 Node.js 的竞争对手，Cloudflare 自己已经有 workerd。
Cloudflare 并没有打算用 Deno 替换 workerd。
Deno 官方宣布：
Deno Runtime 再维护一年，之后停止官方开发。
Deno Deploy 再运行六个月，之后关闭。
Deno 团队转向 Cloudflare Workers 和 Durable Objects 的研发。
这笔交易图什么？
大概判断：Cloudflare 想把 Workers 从一个自家的云计算产品，进一步发展成一种别人也能部署的应用运行平台。
这和 Vite 的收购构成了两个方向：
Vite 让更多开发者愿意使用 Workers；
Deno 团队则帮助 Workers 摆脱对 Cloudflare 自家基础设施的依赖。
商业分析：既然 Cloudflare 靠出租自己的云计算资源赚钱，为什么反而要让别人把 Workers 部署到自己的服务器上？
因为 Cloudflare 认为：允许客户离开，反而能吸引更多客户进来。
举个例子：假设你是一家大企业，准备用 Workers 开发核心业务。你会担心：万一将来 Cloudflare 涨价、服务出问题，我的软件岂不是搬不走？
现在 Cloudflare 想给你两个选择：
付费使用 Cloudflare Workers：不用管理服务器，享受全球网络、自动扩容等服务。
自己部署 Workers：可以掌控基础设施，但服务器、运维、扩容等问题要自己解决。
Cloudflare 赌的是：只要消除了被厂商绑定的顾虑，更多企业就愿意采用 Workers；其中大多数仍会选择省事的付费云服务。
这不是纯粹推测。Cloudflare 在公告中曾经提到过：2022 年向 Shopify 等大客户推销 Workers 时，客户明确要求运行时必须开源，否则根本不会采用。Cloudflare 因此开放了 workerd，甚至表示已经有客户利用它迁离 Cloudflare，但公司仍认为这笔账划算。
所以，Cloudflare 收编 Deno 团队的战略更广大，是降低采用 Workers 的风险，把 Workers 从自家专有云产品逐渐推广成一种通用的软件运行方式。
它想赚的是托管和运营这种运行方式的钱，而不只是依靠技术封闭来留住客户。
2022 年 Cloudflare 就把 workerd 开源了，用户确实可以自行部署。但开源的不是完整的 Workers 云平台。
用户为什么选择 Workers？
主要是三个好处：
省钱：高密度运行 JavaScript，比传统的独立进程部署方式更节约资源。
省事：使用 Cloudflare 托管版，不用自己管理服务器、扩容。
方便开发分布式应用：特别是 Durable Objects，让程序员更容易处理实时通信、数据状态等问题。
这些是 Cloudflare 官方强调的核心优势。
那为什么还要自行部署？
例如，一家企业认可 Workers 的编程方式，但希望使用自己的服务器，而不是向 Cloudflare 租计算资源。
2022 年 workerd 开源后，已经可以这么做。
但当时有一个很大的缺陷：自己部署的 workerd，缺乏完整的分布式管理能力。
举个例子：你有 100 台服务器，准备运行一个使用 Durable Objects 的聊天应用。你需要解决：某个聊天室应该在哪台机器上运行？用户请求如何找到这台机器？机器故障后怎么恢复聊天室的数据和运行状态？在 Cloudflare 托管版里，这些主要由平台负责。
但自己部署 workerd 时，Durable Objects 只有单实例实现，不能直接实现跨服务器的分布式扩展。你得另外解决这些问题。
Cloudflare 在 AI 时代的策略预测
Cloudflare 正在争夺 AI 时代软件生产和运行的基础设施，而不只是传统的云计算市场。
AI 让软件生产成本下降，可能催生远多于过去的应用和 Agent。Cloudflare 希望无论这些软件由人还是 AI 编写，都尽可能采用它的工具链与运行模型。
Cloudflare vs Vercel
Astro：争夺 AI 创建 Web 应用时使用的框架生态。扩大自己的 Web 框架生态，这也是与 Next.js（Vercel）生态的直接肉搏。
VoidZero / Vite：从开发工具链入手，争夺 AI 编写、测试、构建软件时使用的工具链，争夺比单一框架更广泛的开发者入口，
Deno / celld：推动 Workers 成为可自托管的运行标准，形成不同于 Vercel 托管平台的差异化优势
其中 Vite 尤其重要：
如果大量 Coding Agent 都使用 Vite，Cloudflare 就有机会影响 AI 生成的软件最终部署到哪里。
Cloudflare 不一定要打造一个全面超越 Next.js 的框架。它可以通过 Vite 触达所有竞品的框架生态，再争取把这些应用部署到 Workers。
Vercel：从 Next.js 和前端框架、前端部署出发，向 AI Coding、Agent 开发和计算基础设施扩张。
Cloudflare：从网络和云计算基础设施出发，向开发框架、工具链和 AI Coding 生态扩张。
面对人工或是 AI agent，抑或竞争对手，Cloudflare 的最终商业目标没有变：让更多应用采用 Workers，其中一部分转化为 Cloudflare 的付费云计算客户。
总结
Cloudflare 试图从一家提供计算资源的云厂商，变成 AI 时代软件开发工具链和运行标准的重要参与者。

events.title: Discord 在这一波生成式人工智能浪潮中，起到什么角色？

en.title: What Role Has Discord Played in the Generative AI Wave?

text.text: Discord is not the infrastructure layer of this generative AI wave, but in 2022–2024 it was especially prominent as a public testing ground for AI products, a distribution platform, and a community operating system. It seemed to be everywhere.

Midjourney is the clearest example. Early on, it did not even have a conventional standalone product interface. You joined Discord, entered /imagine followed by a prompt in a channel, and the Midjourney bot returned four images. Buttons let you upscale them or generate variations. Discord was effectively Midjourney’s frontend. Midjourney only gradually moved more of the experience to its own website, and Discord remains an official entry point today.
This spared a startup from building a whole stack of features itself:

A traditional AI startup

Model
↓
Backend service
↓
Account system
↓
Chat / input box
↓
Multiplayer community
↓
Permissions
↓
Notifications
↓
User feedback
↓
Product distribution
Early Midjourney instead looked like:

Model + bot
      ↓
   Discord
 ┌─────────────┐
 User system
 Channels
 Community
 Permissions
 Messages
 Image display
 Bot API
 Social distribution
 └─────────────┘
Discord at that stage could even be understood as a very early AI app runtime.
Discord was already much more than simple instant messaging:
Server → Channel → User → Bot → Permissions → Message stream
And generative AI naturally fits this pattern:
A user sends a prompt → a bot processes it → the bot returns generated output.
The two interfaces fit almost perfectly.
More Importantly, It Made Using AI a Public Activity
Midjourney’s early Discord experience was unusual:
You entered:
/imagine cyberpunk Tokyo in the rain
Then everyone could see:
Your prompt
→ How the AI generated the images
→ All four results
→ Which result you selected
→ How you revised your prompt next.
A newcomer did not even need to read a tutorial. They could simply watch others experiment in the channel.
Prompt engineering, showcasing work, tutorials, social sharing, and product use all took place in the same interface.

This was one important reason for Midjourney’s extraordinary early growth. Discord’s own case study says that, after expanding from a small test, Midjourney’s official server quickly reached the then-current limit of about one million members. Discord now lists roughly 18.6 million members on the official server.
This is not quite the same as how ChatGPT spread.
With ChatGPT: I chat privately with the AI → I am impressed → I post a screenshot on Twitter.
With Midjourney and Discord, the interaction with AI itself already happens in a public square.
That naturally creates a loop of watching → imitating → creating → showcasing → sharing again.
Discord also played a substantial role in open-source AI.

Many early Stable Diffusion communities, model developers, plugin authors, and AI artists gathered on Discord. Discord has even publicly stated that Stable Diffusion’s creators first met and collaborated in its communities.
Stability AI’s official Discord subsequently became an important place for model releases, creator discussions, and developer conversations.
The AI image ecosystem of 2022 therefore often divided responsibilities like this:

GitHub
Handles: code

Hugging Face
Handles: models / weights

Discord
Handles:
People
Discussions
Feedback
Tutorials
Prompts
Artwork
Plugins
Model testing
Community
From the perspective of industry history, I think Discord unintentionally became one of generative AI’s first native interaction environments during the early phase of this wave.
It was originally designed for people to talk to people. Yet its combination of bots, slash commands, servers, and channels suddenly fit a new pattern remarkably well: human ↔ AI ↔ human.
That extended the original pattern of human ↔ human.
This explains why, around 2022, so many projects said: Want to try this new AI? Join our Discord.
Many did not even have a formal product yet. The Discord server was the next stop after the website, and the bot was the product.
Within the history of generative AI products that I have been exploring, Discord occupies a distinctive position:

It is not an AI company, a model provider, a compute provider, or a development framework. It was more like a ready-made application environment that happened to exist when generative AI exploded in 2022–2023.
Midjourney × Discord, in particular, deserves its own place in the history of this wave of AI products.

en.excerpt: Discord is not the infrastructure layer of this generative AI wave, but in 2022–2024 it was especially prominent as a public testing ground for AI products, a distribution platform

text.text: Discord 不是这波生成式 AI 的“基础设施”，但在 2022–2024 年尤其像一个AI 产品的公共试验场 + 分发平台 + 社区操作系统。给人一种到处都是它的感觉。
最典型的就是 Midjourney。它早期甚至没有正常意义上的独立产品界面：进入 Discord，在频道里输入
/imagine xxx
，Midjourney Bot 回四张图，再点按钮继续放大、变体。也就是说，Discord 本身就是 Midjourney 的前端。Midjourney 后来才逐步把体验迁到自己的网站；直到今天 Discord 仍然是正式入口之一。
它相当于把一家创业公司原本需要自己做的一大堆东西都省了：

传统 AI 创业公司

模型
↓
后端服务
↓
账号系统
↓
聊天 / 输入框
↓
多人社区
↓
权限
↓
通知
↓
用户反馈
↓
产品传播
Midjourney 早期变成：

模型 + Bot
      ↓
   Discord
 ┌─────────────┐
 用户系统
 Channel
 社区
 权限
 消息
 图片展示
 Bot API
 社交传播
 └─────────────┘
甚至可以把那一阶段的 Discord 理解成一种非常早的
“AI App Runtime”
因为 Discord 本来就不是简单 IM，而是：
Server → Channel → 用户 → Bot → 权限 → 消息流
而生成式 AI 恰好天然适合：
用户发 prompt → Bot 处理 → Bot 返回生成结果。
两者的接口几乎严丝合缝。
更重要的是，它把「使用 AI」变成了公开行为
Midjourney 在 Discord 里的早期体验其实很奇怪：
输入：
/imagine cyberpunk Tokyo in the rain
然后所有人都能看到：
你的 prompt
→ AI 怎么生成
→ 四张结果
→ 你选了哪张
→ 你怎么继续改 prompt。
于是一个新用户根本不用读教程。他就在频道里看别人玩。
所以 prompt engineering、作品展示、教程、社交传播、产品使用本身，全部发生在同一个界面里。
这是 Midjourney 早期增长非常恐怖的重要原因之一。Discord 自己的案例研究称，Midjourney 从小规模测试扩张后，官方服务器很快撞到当时约 100 万成员的服务器上限；今天 Discord 显示其官方服务器已有约 1860 万成员。
这和 ChatGPT 的传播方式还不完全一样。
ChatGPT 是：我和 AI 私聊 → 我觉得牛 → 截图发 Twitter。
Midjourney + Discord 是：我和 AI 交互这件事情本身就在公共广场里发生。
所以它天然自带 观摩 → 模仿 → 创作 → 展示 → 再传播的循环。
Discord 对
开源 AI
的作用也很大。
Stable Diffusion 那批社区、模型开发者、插件作者、AI 艺术家，早期大量聚集在 Discord。Discord 甚至公开说过，Stable Diffusion 的创造者最初就是在 Discord 社区中相识并协作。
Stability AI 自己的官方 Discord 此后也成为模型发布、创作者交流、开发者讨论的重要场所。
于是 2022 年那一波 AI 图像生态里，经常形成：

GitHub
负责：代码

Hugging Face
负责：模型 / 权重

Discord
负责：
人
讨论
反馈
教程
prompt
作品
插件
模型测试
社区
所以从产业史角度，我觉得 Discord 在这波 AI 浪潮的早期：无意中成为了生成式 AI 第一代“原生交互容器”之一。
它本来是给人和人聊天的。结果 Bot + Slash Command + Server + Channel 这套设计，突然非常适合：人 ↔ AI ↔ 人
而不是原来的：人 ↔ 人。
这也是为什么 2022 年左右会出现那么多：“想试这个新 AI？Join our Discord。”
甚至很多项目当时根本没有正式产品，Discord Server 就是官网之后的第二站，Bot 就是产品。
如果放到我一直在梳理的这一波生成式 AI 产品史里，目前会给 Discord 一个挺特殊的位置：
它不是 AI 公司，也不是模型层、算力层或者开发框架；它更像 2022–23 年生成式 AI 爆发时，偶然存在的一块现成的“应用层土壤”。
尤其是 Midjourney × Discord，是这一波 AI 产品史里非常值得单独记的一组组合。

events.title: Supabase 收购 Turso
events.subtitle: Agent 时代的数据库数量爆炸

en.title: Supabase Acquires Turso
en.subtitle: An explosion in database instances in the agent era

text.text: Why the Acquisition?
Supabase creates more than a million databases per week, with roughly 70% of new databases coming from agents and AI tools. Agents are changing the pattern:
Previously: a small number of large, long-running databases.
Now: vast numbers of small databases, created on demand and paused whenever they are not needed.
A typical pattern is one agent, task, or user → one isolated database.
Turso addresses exactly this need: one server can manage millions of small databases, loading them when needed and suspending them otherwise.
How Supabase and Turso Divide Responsibilities
The official announcement says Turso will not replace Postgres.
Turso
SQLite-based approach
Small databases
Huge numbers of instances
Fast creation
Agents and temporary tasks
Supabase
Postgres-based approach
More complex applications
Larger data volumes
A complete backend platform
The broad path is small agent databases → Turso → Supabase/Postgres as requirements become more complex. The products initially remain separate and will gradually become more integrated.
Turso founder Glauber Costa will join Supabase to lead agent-related services.
What Exactly Is Turso?
Its history: SQLite → a fork called libSQL; a Rust rewrite called Limbo → Turso Database.
Turso initially forked SQLite directly to create libSQL.

As its ambitions expanded, continuing to modify SQLite became awkward. The team built a new SQLite-compatible database from scratch in Rust, retaining SQLite’s lightweight experience while redesigning the internal architecture.
Why Not Keep Modifying SQLite?
SQLite’s core purpose is to be a local, embedded, single-file database requiring no administration.
It was not designed for cloud-era requirements such as multitenancy, distributed operation, branching, huge numbers of database instances, or agent databases.

SQLite also follows an unusual open-source model: it is open source, but not open contribution. A very small team has maintained its core for years, generally does not accept ordinary pull requests, and places exceptional emphasis on stability and long-term compatibility.

Turso wanted to add many capabilities quickly: asynchronous I/O, concurrent writes, vector search, WASM, branching, replication, cloud tenancy, and management of vast numbers of databases. These goals naturally differ from SQLite’s development philosophy.
SQLite is clearly reluctant to substantially restructure its core architecture to meet these cloud-era requirements.
Why Rewrite It in Rust?
Rust’s memory-safety advantages over C are real, but they are certainly not the central reason.

SQLite already has exceptionally high engineering quality. Its test code is roughly hundreds of times larger than its source code, its 100% branch coverage is comparable to aviation software standards, and its most comprehensive test suite is proprietary.
The story cannot simply be reduced to SQLite being unsafe because it uses C and Turso fixing that by using Rust.

The more fundamental reason is that Turso wanted a codebase it could fully control and evolve freely. Rust’s memory safety, asynchronous capabilities, and modern engineering ecosystem fit that goal well.
Summary
Supabase’s acquisition of Turso is a bet on agents causing an explosion in the number of database instances, rather than merely needing larger databases.
SQLite provides a lightweight database model. Turso aims to extend that model into the cloud and agent era.
Related
Databricks Acquires Electric
AWS Acquires DuckDB

text.text: 为什么收购
Supabase 每周创建超过 100 万个数据库，约 70% 新数据库来自 Agent / AI 工具。Agent 带来的变化：
过去：少量、大型、长期运行的数据库。
现在：海量、小型、按需创建、随时暂停的数据库。
典型模式：1 个 Agent / 1 个任务 / 1 个用户 → 1 个独立数据库。
Turso 正好解决这个问题：一台服务器可以管理数百万个小数据库，需要时加载，不需要时暂停。
Supabase + Turso 如何分工
官方表示不会用 Turso 替代 Postgres。
Turso
SQLite 路线
小数据库
海量实例
快速创建
Agent / 临时任务
Supabase
Postgres 路线
更复杂业务
更大的数据规模
完整后端能力
大致路线：小型 Agent 数据库 → Turso → 需求变复杂后进入 Supabase / Postgres。目前两边产品暂时独立，之后逐步打通。
Turso 创始人 Glauber Costa 将加入 Supabase，负责 Agent 相关服务。
Turso 到底是什么
历史：SQLite → fork → libSQL，Rust 重写 Limbo → Turso Database
最初 Turso 直接 fork SQLite，做 libSQL。
后来发现想加的东西越来越多，继续改 SQLite 很别扭，于是用 Rust 从头重写了一个 SQLite 兼容数据库：保留了 SQLite 的轻量体验 + 重做内部架构。
为什么不能直接继续改 SQLite
SQLite 的核心定位：本地、嵌入式、单文件、零运维数据库。
它不是为了解决这些云时代的问题而设计的：云多租户 / 分布式 / branch / 海量数据库实例 / Agent 数据库。
而且 SQLite 是一种很特殊的开源项目：open source，但不是 open contribution。核心代码长期由很小的团队维护，基本不接受普通 PR，极度重视稳定性和长期兼容。
Turso 想快速加入大量新能力，这和 SQLite 的开发哲学天然有冲突：异步 I/O、并发写入、向量搜索、WASM、branch、replication、cloud tenancy、海量数据库管理。
SQLite 显然不愿意了这些云时代需求，大幅重构自己的核心架构。
为什么用 Rust 重写
“Rust 比 C 安全”是真的，但肯定不是最核心原因。
SQLite 本身工程质量极高：测试代码量约为源码数百倍，分支覆盖率做到航空软件级别的 100% branch coverage，最完整测试体系甚至闭源。
所以不能简单理解成：SQLite 用 C 不安全，Turso 用 Rust 修复它。
真正原因更接近：Turso 想要一个自己完全控制、可以自由演进的代码库。Rust 的内存安全、异步能力和现代工程生态非常适合这个目标。
总结
Supabase 收购 Turso，押注的不是“Agent 需要更大的数据库”，而是“Agent 会让数据库实例数量暴涨”。
SQLite 解决的是轻量数据库；Turso 想把这种轻量模型扩展到云和 Agent 时代。
相关：
Databricks 收购 Electric
AWS 收购 duckdb

events.title: Databricks 收购 Electric
events.subtitle: 把 Postgres 数据同步到 App / Agent 身边

en.title: Databricks Acquires Electric
en.subtitle: Bringing Postgres data closer to apps and agents

text.text: What Is Electric?

Electric, formerly ElectricSQL and legally Electric DB Limited, is not a conventional database company. Its core offering combines a real-time synchronization layer for Postgres with a local Postgres runtime.
In August 2026, Electric joined Databricks and became part of the Neon team.
Electric’s Core Products
PGlite
A lightweight WebAssembly build of Postgres that runs directly in browsers, apps, sandboxes, serverless environments, and agent execution environments.
In other words, Postgres does not have to run only on a remote database server. It can be embedded directly in an application.
Over the past year, PGlite’s weekly downloads grew from roughly 1 million to 13 million.
Electric Sync
Continuously synchronizes the required subset of a central Postgres database to browsers, phones, local databases, sandboxes, and agents.
Core flow: Postgres → Electric Sync → Client / Agent / PGlite.
Electric captures changes through Postgres logical replication, then continuously pushes selected subsets of the data to clients.
What Problem Does It Solve?
The traditional model is Client / Agent → API → Backend → Postgres. Every data request requires a remote trip to the backend and database.
Electric’s approach is to synchronize the required data close to the execution environment first, let the application read locally, and continuously deliver changes from Postgres.
The benefits include low latency, real-time interfaces, offline capabilities, less synchronization code, and shared state across multiple clients and agents.
This kind of system is often called a sync engine, a local-first data layer, or a reactive data layer.
An important clarification: Electric is not currently a complete bidirectional synchronization database.
Electric Sync currently focuses on read synchronization from Postgres to clients.
Writes generally still follow Client → API / Server Action / Backend → Postgres. Changes then flow from Postgres → Electric → other clients and agents.
It is therefore misleading to draw the architecture simply as PGlite ⇄ Electric ⇄ Postgres.
A more accurate description is:
Writes: App → Backend → Postgres.
Reads and real-time updates: Postgres → Electric → App / Agent.
Earlier Electric versions supported more extensive local-first, bidirectional replication, but the product’s direction subsequently changed substantially.
Why Did Databricks Acquire It?
The timeline makes the strategy clear:
2025: Databricks acquires Neon, obtaining serverless Postgres capabilities such as scale-to-zero and branching.
2025: Databricks launches Lakebase, using Neon technology to add an OLTP/operational database layer for AI applications and agents.
2026: Electric joins Databricks and Neon, adding local Postgres and real-time synchronization.
The resulting architecture is:
Lakebase / Neon = cloud-hosted serverless Postgres.
PGlite = local Postgres close to the agent or application.
Electric = the real-time data synchronization layer between them.
Summary
Neon addresses how to make Postgres in the cloud better suited to agents.
Electric addresses how to bring Postgres data close to those agents.

This also explains why Electric joined the Neon team directly rather than becoming a separate Databricks product line. Electric later explicitly argued that synchronization works better as a fundamental Backend-as-a-Service capability than as a complete standalone platform.

Electric 的核心产品是
PGlite
把 Postgres 编译成轻量的 WebAssembly 版本，可以直接运行在：浏览器 / App / sandbox / serverless / Agent 执行环境
可以理解成：Postgres 不一定只能跑在远程数据库服务器里，也可以直接塞进应用内部。
过去一年，PGlite 周下载量从约 100 万增长到 1300 万。
Electric Sync
负责把中央 Postgres 中需要的部分数据持续同步到：浏览器 / 手机 / 本地数据库 / sandbox / Agent
核心结构：Postgres → Electric Sync → Client / Agent / PGlite
Electric 通过 Postgres logical replication 获取数据库变化，再把指定的数据子集持续推给客户端。
它解决什么问题
传统模式：Client / Agent → API → Backend → Postgres。每次需要数据，都要远程访问后端和数据库。
Electric 的思路是：先把需要的数据同步到执行环境附近 → 应用直接在本地读取 → Postgres 变化持续同步过来。
好处：低延迟 / 实时 UI / 离线能力 / 少写大量同步代码 / 多客户端与多 Agent 状态同步
这类东西通常叫：sync engine / local-first data layer / reactive data layer
一个易误解的地方：Electric 目前不是完整“双向同步数据库”
当前 Electric Sync 的重点是：Postgres → Client 的读同步。
写入通常仍然：Client → API / Server Action / Backend → Postgres。然后：Postgres → Electric → 其他 Client / Agent
所以不能简单画成：PGlite ⇄ Electric ⇄ Postgres
更准确的描述是：
写：App → Backend → Postgres
读 / 实时更新：Postgres → Electric → App / Agent
Electric 早期版本做过更完整的 local-first 双向复制，但后来产品方向发生过明显变化。
为什么 Databricks 要买它
时间线非常清楚：
2025：Databricks 收购 Neon
→ 获得 serverless Postgres、scale-to-zero、branching 等数据库能力。
2025：推出 Lakebase
→ 用 Neon 技术给 Databricks 补上 OLTP / operational database，面向 AI App 和 Agent。
2026：Electric 加入 Databricks / Neon
→ 再补上 本地 Postgres + realtime sync。
于是整个结构变成：
Lakebase / Neon
= 云端 Serverless Postgres
PGlite
= Agent / App 身边的本地 Postgres
Electric
= 两者之间的实时数据同步层
总结：
Neon 解决“云里的 Postgres 怎么更适合 Agent”，
Electric 解决“怎么把 Postgres 数据送到 Agent 身边”。
这也是为什么 Electric 加入后不是独立做一条 Databricks 产品线，而是直接并入 Neon 团队：Electric 自己后来也明确认为，sync 更适合作为 Backend-as-a-Service 的一个基础能力，而不是单独做成完整平台。
